about: Relates a creative work, event, or term to the subject matter or topic it describes. Also called "subject matter of", "topic of", "focuses on", "covers". Examples: [Book "The Hobbit" - about - "Middle-earth"], [Lecture - about - "Quantum Physics"], [Article - about - "Climate Change"]. Distinct from mainEntity, which is the primary, singular topic that the page or work is explicitly a representation of.
abridged: Relates a book to a boolean value indicating whether it is a shortened or condensed version of the original text. Also called "is condensed", "is shortened", "abridgement status". Examples: [Novel "War and Peace" - abridged - true], [Audiobook "Moby Dick" - abridged - false], [Textbook - abridged - true].
abstract: Relates a creative work to a short text summary that outlines its main points and findings. Also called "summary of", "synopsis of", "executive summary". Examples: [Research Paper - abstract - "This study explores..."], [Thesis - abstract - "An analysis of..."], [Patent - abstract - "A device for..."]. Distinct from description, which is a general, non-academic description of any item.
accelerationTime: Relates a vehicle to the quantitative duration required to accelerate from a starting speed to a target speed. Also called "zero to sixty time", "acceleration duration", "time to speed". Examples: [Sports Car - accelerationTime - "3.2 seconds"], [Electric Sedan - accelerationTime - "4.5 seconds"], [Motorcycle - accelerationTime - "2.8 seconds"].
acceptedAnswer: Relates a question to the answer or list of answers that has been selected as the best or correct response. Also called "best answer", "selected answer", "resolved answer". Examples: [Forum Question - acceptedAnswer - Answer "Use the map function"], [StackOverflow Post - acceptedAnswer - Answer "Install package X"], [FAQ Question - acceptedAnswer - Answer "Yes, we ship worldwide"].
acceptedOffer: Relates an order to the specific offer, including product and price combinations, that was selected and purchased. Also called "purchased offer", "selected offer", "included offer". Examples: [Order #102 - acceptedOffer - Offer "Laptop with 10% discount"], [Subscription Order - acceptedOffer - Offer "Monthly Premium Plan"], [Ticket Order - acceptedOffer - Offer "VIP Pass"].
acceptedPaymentMethod: Relates an organization, demand, or offer to the payment methods it accepts for transactions. Also called "payment options", "payment methods accepted", "takes payment via". Examples: [Online Store - acceptedPaymentMethod - "Credit Card"], [Local Cafe - acceptedPaymentMethod - "Cash"], [Subscription Offer - acceptedPaymentMethod - "PayPal"].
acceptsReservations: Relates a food establishment to a boolean, URL, or text indicating whether it allows customers to book tables in advance. Also called "takes bookings", "reservation policy", "booking accepted". Examples: [Italian Restaurant - acceptsReservations - true], [Bistro - acceptsReservations - "https://bistro.com/book"], [Fast Food Joint - acceptsReservations - false].
accessCode: Relates a delivery event to the password, PIN, or code required to retrieve or complete the delivery. Also called "delivery PIN", "locker code", "pickup password". Examples: [Locker Delivery - accessCode - "98421"], [Package Dropoff - accessCode - "A7B9"], [Secure Shipment - accessCode - "PASS123"].
accessMode: Relates a creative work to the human sensory or cognitive faculty required to perceive or process its content. Also called "sensory mode", "perception mode", "cognitive access mode". Examples: [Audiobook - accessMode - "auditory"], [E-book - accessMode - "visual"], [Braille Novel - accessMode - "tactile"].
accessModeSufficient: Relates a creative work to a list of sensory or cognitive access modes that, individually or combined, are sufficient to fully comprehend the content. Also called "sufficient access modes", "accessibility combinations", "adequate sensory modes". Examples: [Video with Captions - accessModeSufficient - "visual, auditory"], [Silent Film - accessModeSufficient - "visual"], [Podcast - accessModeSufficient - "auditory"].
accessibilityAPI: Relates a creative work to the specific accessibility API with which it is compatible. Also called "compatible accessibility API", "supported screen reader API", "accessibility interface". Examples: [Web App - accessibilityAPI - "ARIA"], [Windows Software - accessibilityAPI - "UI Automation"], [iOS App - accessibilityAPI - "iOS Accessibility"].
accessibilityControl: Relates a creative work to the input methods that are sufficient to fully control and navigate the resource. Also called "input control method", "accessibility input", "control mechanism". Examples: [Interactive Game - accessibilityControl - "keyboard"], [E-learning Module - accessibilityControl - "voiceInput"], [Web Page - accessibilityControl - "switchControl"].
accessibilityFeature: Relates a creative work to the specific features or enhancements included to make it accessible to users with disabilities. Also called "accessibility enhancement", "accessible feature", "assistive feature". Examples: [Video - accessibilityFeature - "captions"], [E-book - accessibilityFeature - "alternativeText"], [Document - accessibilityFeature - "taggedPDF"].
accessibilityHazard: Relates a creative work to any physiological hazard it presents, such as flashing lights that could trigger seizures. Also called "sensory hazard", "accessibility warning", "physiological danger". Examples: [Action Video Game - accessibilityHazard - "flashingHazard"], [Audio Track - accessibilityHazard - "soundVolumeHazard"], [Web Page - accessibilityHazard - "motionSimulationHazard"].
accessibilitySummary: Relates a creative work to a human-readable text summary describing its overall accessibility features or deficiencies. Also called "accessibility overview", "accessibility statement", "assistive summary". Examples: [Online Textbook - accessibilitySummary - "Contains alt text for all images but lacks audio descriptions."], [Video Course - accessibilitySummary - "Fully captioned with transcripts provided."], [Interactive Map - accessibilitySummary - "Not keyboard navigable."].
accommodationCategory: Relates an accommodation to its real estate classification or category. Also called "property type", "accommodation class", "real estate category". Examples: [Apartment 4B - accommodationCategory - "Condominium"], [Beach Villa - accommodationCategory - "SingleFamilyResidence"], [Studio Unit - accommodationCategory - "Apartment"].
accommodationFloorPlan: Relates an accommodation or residence to its structural floor plan. Also called "layout plan", "floor layout", "apartment floorplan". Examples: [Apartment 3A - accommodationFloorPlan - FloorPlan "2 Bed 2 Bath"], [Townhouse - accommodationFloorPlan - FloorPlan "Triplex Layout"], [Studio Flat - accommodationFloorPlan - FloorPlan "Open Concept"].
accountId: Relates an invoice to the unique identifier of the account to which the payment should be applied. Also called "account number", "billing account ID", "customer account code". Examples: [Utility Invoice - accountId - "ACT-90812"], [Internet Bill - accountId - "11029384"], [Consulting Invoice - accountId - "ACCT-CORP-01"].
accountMinimumInflow: Relates a bank account to the minimum monetary amount that must be deposited into it each month. Also called "minimum monthly deposit", "required monthly inflow", "minimum deposit requirement". Examples: [Checking Account - accountMinimumInflow - "$1,000 USD"], [Premium Savings - accountMinimumInflow - "€2,500 EUR"], [Student Account - accountMinimumInflow - "$0 USD"].
accountOverdraftLimit: Relates a bank account to the maximum monetary amount the bank allows the account holder to borrow when the balance reaches zero. Also called "overdraft protection limit", "overdraft line", "allowed negative balance". Examples: [Checking Account - accountOverdraftLimit - "$500 USD"], [Business Account - accountOverdraftLimit - "£5,000 GBP"], [Student Account - accountOverdraftLimit - "$100 USD"].
accountablePerson: Relates a creative work to the person who is legally responsible or accountable for its content. Also called "legally responsible person", "accountable party", "responsible editor". Examples: [News Article - accountablePerson - Person "Jane Doe"], [Corporate Report - accountablePerson - Person "John Smith"], [Medical Guide - accountablePerson - Person "Dr. Alice Green"].
acquireLicensePage: Relates a creative work to a web page or resource detailing how to purchase or acquire a license for it. Also called "licensing page", "buy license link", "how to license". Examples: [Stock Photo - acquireLicensePage - "https://photos.com/license/123"], [Software Library - acquireLicensePage - "https://github.com/lib/license"], [Digital Album - acquireLicensePage - "https://band.com/licensing"].
acquiredFrom: Relates ownership information to the person or organization from whom the product or asset was obtained. Also called "purchased from", "obtained from", "sourced from". Examples: [Used Car Ownership - acquiredFrom - Person "Bob Smith"], [Art Collection - acquiredFrom - "Sotheby's Auction House"], [Real Estate Deed - acquiredFrom - "City Developers Corp"].
acrissCode: Relates a vehicle, such as a car or coach, to its standard ACRISS Car Classification Code. Also called "car classification code", "ACRISS category", "rental car code". Examples: [Rental Sedan - acrissCode - "CDMR"], [SUV - acrissCode - "IFAR"], [Luxury Convertible - acrissCode - "XTAR"].
actionAccessibilityRequirement: Relates a consume action to the specific access requirements or specifications that must be met to perform it. Also called "access requirements", "prerequisites for action", "consumption conditions". Examples: [Watch Movie Action - actionAccessibilityRequirement - ActionAccessSpecification "Subscription Required"], [Download File Action - actionAccessibilityRequirement - ActionAccessSpecification "Age Verification"], [Enter Event Action - actionAccessibilityRequirement - ActionAccessSpecification "Ticket Purchase"].
actionApplication: Relates an entry point to the software application that can execute or complete the requested action. Also called "handling application", "executing software", "target app". Examples: [Search EntryPoint - actionApplication - "Google Search App"], [Play Music EntryPoint - actionApplication - "Spotify App"], [Open Document EntryPoint - actionApplication - "Adobe Acrobat"]. Distinct from application, which is a more generic relation for associated software.
actionOption: Relates a choose action to the available options or choices presented to the user. Also called "choice option", "available choice", "selection option". Examples: [Vote Action - actionOption - "Option A"], [Select Color Action - actionOption - "Blue"], [Choose Plan Action - actionOption - "Premium Plan"].
actionPlatform: Relates an entry point to the high-level digital platform or operating system where the action can be performed. Also called "supported platform", "action operating system", "target platform". Examples: [Watch Video EntryPoint - actionPlatform - "Android"], [Edit Document EntryPoint - actionPlatform - "Web Browser"], [Play Game EntryPoint - actionPlatform - "iOS"].
actionProcess: Relates an action to the step-by-step instructions or how-to guide describing how the action was or should be performed. Also called "execution process", "action steps", "how-to process". Examples: [Bake Cake Action - actionProcess - HowTo "Chocolate Cake Recipe"], [Assemble Desk Action - actionProcess - HowTo "Assembly Manual"], [Install Software Action - actionProcess - HowTo "Setup Guide"].
actionStatus: Relates an action to its current state of execution or disposition. Also called "execution state", "status of action", "progress status". Examples: [Order Delivery Action - actionStatus - "CompletedActionStatus"], [Download Action - actionStatus - "ActiveActionStatus"], [Payment Action - actionStatus - "FailedActionStatus"].
actionableFeedbackPolicy: Relates an organization or news media organization to its policy regarding public engagement and feedback on its coverage or activities. Also called "feedback policy", "public engagement policy", "reader feedback guidelines". Examples: [Times Newspaper - actionableFeedbackPolicy - "https://times.com/feedback-policy"], [Local News Station - actionableFeedbackPolicy - "https://localnews.org/engagement"], [Global Media Corp - actionableFeedbackPolicy - PolicyDocument].
activeIngredient: Relates a dietary supplement, drug, or substance to its active chemical or biological component. Also called "active component", "medicinal ingredient", "active substance". Examples: [Aspirin - activeIngredient - "Acetylsalicylic acid"], [Tylenol - activeIngredient - "Acetaminophen"], [Sleep Supplement - activeIngredient - "Melatonin"].
activityDuration: Relates an exercise plan to the length of time recommended for engaging in the physical activity. Also called "exercise duration", "workout length", "time per session". Examples: [Cardio Plan - activityDuration - "30 minutes"], [Yoga Routine - activityDuration - "1 hour"], [HIIT Workout - activityDuration - "15 minutes"].
activityFrequency: Relates an exercise plan to how often the physical activity should be performed. Also called "exercise frequency", "workout frequency", "how often to exercise". Examples: [Strength Training - activityFrequency - "3 times per week"], [Daily Walk - activityFrequency - "Once per day"], [Stretching Plan - activityFrequency - "Every morning"].
actor: Relates a creative work, episode, movie, or event to a performing group or person who plays a role in it. Also called "cast member", "starring", "performer". Examples: [Movie "Inception" - actor - Person "Leonardo DiCaprio"], [Play "Hamlet" - actor - "The Royal Shakespeare Company"], [TV Episode - actor - Person "Bryan Cranston"]. Distinct from actors, which specifically restricts the range to individual Person entities.
actors: Relates a creative work, episode, movie, or series to an individual person who performs as an actor in it. Also called "cast member", "performer", "starring person". Examples: [Movie "The Matrix" - actors - Person "Keanu Reeves"], [TV Show "Friends" - actors - Person "Jennifer Aniston"], [Video Game - actors - Person "Ashley Johnson"]. Distinct from actor, which can also accept a PerformingGroup as its object.
addOn: Relates a base offer to an additional offer that can only be purchased in combination with it. Also called "upsell offer", "supplementary offer", "extra add-on". Examples: [Flight Ticket Offer - addOn - Offer "Extra Baggage Allowance"], [Software Subscription - addOn - Offer "Premium Support"], [Console Offer - addOn - Offer "Extended Warranty"].
additionalName: Relates a person to any additional name they have, such as a middle name or patronymic. Also called "middle name", "patronymic", "secondary name". Examples: [Person "John Fitzgerald Kennedy" - additionalName - "Fitzgerald"], [Person "George Walker Bush" - additionalName - "Walker"], [Person "Arthur Conan Doyle" - additionalName - "Conan"].
additionalNumberOfGuests: Relates an RSVP action to the number of extra guests who will attend the event alongside the invitee. Also called "plus ones", "extra guests count", "additional attendees". Examples: [Wedding RSVP - additionalNumberOfGuests - 1], [Dinner RSVP - additionalNumberOfGuests - 2], [Party RSVP - additionalNumberOfGuests - 0].
additionalProperty: Relates an entity, such as a product, place, or offer, to a custom property-value pair representing an extra characteristic not covered by standard schema properties. Also called "custom attribute", "extra characteristic", "specification property". Examples: [Laptop Product - additionalProperty - PropertyValue "RAM Speed: 3200MHz"], [Hotel Room - additionalProperty - PropertyValue "View: Ocean View"], [Bicycle - additionalProperty - PropertyValue "Frame Material: Carbon Fiber"].
additionalType: Relates any entity to an additional, more specific RDF class or type URI. Also called "rdf:type", "extra type", "semantic class". Examples: [Local Business - additionalType - "https://schema.org/Restaurant"], [Book - additionalType - "http://vocab.org/BookType"], [Product - additionalType - "https://example.com/CustomProductClass"].
additionalVariable: Relates an exercise plan to any additional instructions or variables, such as exercise order or progression details, prescribed to the patient. Also called "exercise variable", "workout progression", "additional prescription detail". Examples: [Rehab Plan - additionalVariable - "Perform exercises in order listed."], [Weight Training - additionalVariable - "Increase weight by 5 lbs every week."], [Cardio Plan - additionalVariable - "Maintain heart rate between 120-140 bpm."].
address: Relates a place, organization, person, or coordinates to its physical postal address. Also called "postal address", "location address", "mailing address". Examples: [Store - address - "1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy, Mountain View, CA"], [Person - address - PostalAddress "123 Main St"], [Eiffel Tower - address - PostalAddress "Champ de Mars, Paris"].
addressCountry: Relates a postal address, region, or coordinates to the country in which it is located. Also called "country", "nation", "country code". Examples: [PostalAddress - addressCountry - "US"], [GeoCoordinates - addressCountry - Country "Canada"], [DefinedRegion - addressCountry - "FR"].
addressLocality: Relates a postal address to the city, town, or locality in which it is situated. Also called "city", "town", "locality". Examples: [PostalAddress - addressLocality - "Mountain View"], [PostalAddress - addressLocality - "London"], [PostalAddress - addressLocality - "Tokyo"].
addressRegion: Relates a postal address or region to the administrative area, state, or province in which it is located. Also called "state", "province", "region". Examples: [PostalAddress - addressRegion - "California"], [PostalAddress - addressRegion - "Ontario"], [PostalAddress - addressRegion - "Bavaria"].
administrationRoute: Relates a drug to the path or route by which it is taken into the body. Also called "route of administration", "how drug is taken", "delivery route". Examples: [Insulin - administrationRoute - "subcutaneous"], [Ibuprofen - administrationRoute - "oral"], [Eye Drops - administrationRoute - "ophthalmic"].
advanceBookingRequirement: Relates an offer or demand to the minimum duration of time required between booking and the actual service or resource usage. Also called "booking lead time", "advance notice required", "prior booking duration". Examples: [Hotel Offer - advanceBookingRequirement - "24 hours"], [Car Rental - advanceBookingRequirement - "2 days"], [Catering Service - advanceBookingRequirement - "1 week"].
adverseOutcome: Relates a medical device or therapeutic procedure to a potential complication, side effect, or negative health outcome. Also called "side effect", "complication", "negative outcome". Examples: [Surgery - adverseOutcome - MedicalEntity "Infection"], [Pacemaker - adverseOutcome - MedicalEntity "Device Malfunction"], [Chemotherapy - adverseOutcome - MedicalEntity "Nausea"]. Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is reserved for life-threatening or severe complications.
affectedBy: Relates a medical test to a drug or substance that can alter or interfere with its results. Also called "interfered with by", "influenced by", "test interference drug". Examples: [Blood Sugar Test - affectedBy - Drug "Metformin"], [Thyroid Test - affectedBy - Drug "Biotin"], [Liver Panel - affectedBy - Drug "Acetaminophen"].
affiliation: Relates a person to an organization, such as a school, club, or employer, with which they are formally associated. Also called "affiliated with", "member of", "associated organization". Examples: [Professor - affiliation - "Stanford University"], [Athlete - affiliation - "Los Angeles Lakers"], [Researcher - affiliation - "CERN"].
afterMedia: Relates a how-to direction to a media object or URL showing the expected state or outcome after performing the step. Also called "after image", "completed step media", "post-step visual". Examples: [HowToDirection "Paint the wall" - afterMedia - ImageObject "Painted Wall"], [HowToDirection "Fold the paper" - afterMedia - VideoObject "Folded Origami"], [HowToDirection "Assemble legs" - afterMedia - "https://manuals.com/step3_after.jpg"].
agent: Relates an action to the person or organization that performs, drives, or executes it. Also called "performer", "actor of action", "executed by". Examples: [Write Action - agent - Person "Stephen King"], [Donate Action - agent - Organization "Red Cross"], [Repair Action - agent - Person "Bob the Mechanic"].
agentInteractionStatistic: Relates an organization or person to an interaction counter tracking their completed interactions in a specific role. Also called "interaction stats", "agent activity count", "engagement statistics". Examples: [Customer Support Agent - agentInteractionStatistic - InteractionCounter "150 resolved tickets"], [Seller - agentInteractionStatistic - InteractionCounter "500 sales"], [Influencer - agentInteractionStatistic - InteractionCounter "10k posts"].
aggregateElement: Relates an item list to a prototype element used to hold aggregate information like ratings or offers for the items in the list. Also called "prototype element", "aggregate item", "list prototype". Examples: [Product List - aggregateElement - Product "Generic Laptop Prototype"], [Hotel List - aggregateElement - Hotel "Standard Room Prototype"], [Course List - aggregateElement - Course "Class Prototype"].
aggregateRating: Relates an entity, such as a product, place, or creative work, to its overall rating based on a collection of reviews or individual ratings. Also called "average rating", "overall rating", "review score". Examples: [Book "The Hobbit" - aggregateRating - AggregateRating "4.8 stars based on 1200 reviews"], [Restaurant - aggregateRating - AggregateRating "4.5 rating"], [Product - aggregateRating - AggregateRating "4.2 out of 5"].
aircraft: Relates a flight to the specific vehicle or model of aircraft used. Also called "plane model", "flight vehicle", "aircraft type". Examples: [Flight UA102 - aircraft - "Boeing 777"], [Flight LH430 - aircraft - Vehicle "Airbus A350"], [Private Flight - aircraft - "Gulfstream G650"].
album: Relates a music group or artist to a music album they produced. Also called "music album", "produced album", "released album". Examples: [MusicGroup "The Beatles" - album - MusicAlbum "Abbey Road"], [Artist "Taylor Swift" - album - MusicAlbum "Midnights"], [Band "Pink Floyd" - album - MusicAlbum "The Dark Side of the Moon"]. Distinct from albums, which is a plural collection relation.
albumProductionType: Relates a music album to its production classification, such as a studio, live, or soundtrack album. Also called "production type", "album format", "recording type". Examples: [Album "Abbey Road" - albumProductionType - "StudioAlbum"], [Album "MTV Unplugged" - albumProductionType - "LiveAlbum"], [Album "Star Wars OST" - albumProductionType - "Soundtrack"].
albumRelease: Relates a music album to a specific release of that album. Also called "album release version", "released edition", "music release". Examples: [Album "Thriller" - albumRelease - MusicRelease "1982 Vinyl Release"], [Album "Abbey Road" - albumRelease - MusicRelease "2019 Remastered CD"], [Album "Midnights" - albumRelease - MusicRelease "Digital Deluxe Edition"].
albumReleaseType: Relates a music album to its release format classification, such as a single, EP, or full album. Also called "release type", "album format type", "release classification". Examples: [Album "Yellow Submarine" - albumReleaseType - "AlbumRelease"], [Album "Jar of Flies" - albumReleaseType - "EPRelease"], [Album "Hey Jude" - albumReleaseType - "SingleRelease"].
albums: Relates a music group or artist to a collection of music albums they have released. Also called "discography", "album collection", "released albums". Examples: [MusicGroup "Coldplay" - albums - MusicAlbum "Parachutes"], [Band "U2" - albums - MusicAlbum "The Joshua Tree"], [Artist "Adele" - albums - MusicAlbum "21"]. Distinct from album, which typically links to a single primary album.
alcoholWarning: Relates a drug to precautions, warnings, or contraindications regarding the consumption of alcohol while taking it. Also called "alcohol precaution", "drinking warning", "alcohol interaction warning". Examples: [Metronidazole - alcoholWarning - "Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication."], [Acetaminophen - alcoholWarning - "Severe liver damage may occur if taken with alcohol."], [Xanax - alcoholWarning - "Avoid alcohol due to increased drowsiness."].
algorithm: Relates a medical risk score to the specific algorithm, rules, or mathematical formula used to calculate it. Also called "calculation rules", "scoring algorithm", "risk formula". Examples: [CHADS2 Score - algorithm - "1 point for Congestive heart failure, 1 for Hypertension..."], [Framingham Risk Score - algorithm - "Multi-variable statistical model based on age, cholesterol..."], [MELD Score - algorithm - "Logarithmic formula using bilirubin, creatinine, and INR."].
alignmentType: Relates an alignment object to the category of alignment between a learning resource and an educational framework node. Also called "educational alignment category", "framework alignment type", "curriculum alignment". Examples: [AlignmentObject - alignmentType - "requires"], [AlignmentObject - alignmentType - "readingLevel"], [AlignmentObject - alignmentType - "educationalSubject"].
alternateName: Relates any entity to an alternative name, alias, or pseudonym. Also called "alias", "pseudonym", "otherwise known as". Examples: [Person "Samuel Clemens" - alternateName - "Mark Twain"], [City "New York" - alternateName - "The Big Apple"], [Company "Alphabet Inc." - alternateName - "Google"].
alternativeHeadline: Relates a creative work to a secondary title, sub-headline, or alternative headline. Also called "sub-headline", "secondary title", "sub-title". Examples: [News Article - alternativeHeadline - "Local Hero Saves Dog from River"], [Blog Post - alternativeHeadline - "A Step-by-Step Guide for Beginners"], [Book - alternativeHeadline - "The Boy Who Lived"].
alternativeOf: Relates a gene to another gene that is a variation or allele of it. Also called "gene variation", "allele of", "alternative gene". Examples: [Gene BRCA1-v1 - alternativeOf - Gene BRCA1], [Gene ALDH2*2 - alternativeOf - Gene ALDH2], [Gene APOE4 - alternativeOf - Gene APOE].
alumni: Relates an educational organization or other organization to a person who graduated from or attended it. Also called "graduates", "former students", "alumni members". Examples: [Harvard University - alumni - Person "Bill Gates"], [Stanford University - alumni - Person "Larry Page"], [High School - alumni - Person "Jane Doe"]. Distinct from alumniOf, which is the inverse relation mapping a Person to their school.
alumniOf: Relates a person to an educational organization or other organization they graduated from or attended. Also called "graduated from", "attended school at", "former student of". Examples: [Person "Barack Obama" - alumniOf - "Columbia University"], [Person "Elon Musk" - alumniOf - "University of Pennsylvania"], [Person "Emma Watson" - alumniOf - "Brown University"]. Distinct from alumni, which is the inverse relation mapping an organization to its graduates.
amenityFeature: Relates an accommodation, floor plan, lodging business, or place to an amenity feature, characteristic, or service it offers. Also called "amenity", "room feature", "property amenity". Examples: [Hotel Room - amenityFeature - LocationFeatureSpecification "Free Wi-Fi"], [Apartment - amenityFeature - LocationFeatureSpecification "In-unit Laundry"], [Campsite - amenityFeature - LocationFeatureSpecification "Fire Pit"].
amount: Relates a financial specification, investment, loan, grant, or money transfer to the monetary amount or number of currency units involved. Also called "monetary value", "sum of money", "transaction amount". Examples: [MoneyTransfer - amount - "$150 USD"], [MonetaryGrant - amount - "€50,000 EUR"], [Loan - amount - "$10,000 USD"].
amountOfThisGood: Relates a type and quantity node to the specific quantity of goods included in an offer. Also called "quantity of goods", "good quantity", "number of items". Examples: [Bulk Offer Node - amountOfThisGood - 12], [Twin Pack Node - amountOfThisGood - 2], [Single Item Node - amountOfThisGood - 1].
announcementLocation: Relates a special announcement to a specific civic structure or local business associated with it. Also called "associated facility", "announcement venue", "relevant location". Examples: [Vaccine Announcement - announcementLocation - CivicStructure "City Health Clinic"], [Store Hours Announcement - announcementLocation - LocalBusiness "Downtown Grocery"], [Testing Announcement - announcementLocation - CivicStructure "County Fairgrounds"].
annualPercentageRate: Relates a financial product to its annual percentage rate (APR) charged for borrowing or earned by investing. Also called "APR", "annual interest rate", "yearly cost of funds". Examples: [Credit Card - annualPercentageRate - "18.9%"], [Mortgage Loan - annualPercentageRate - "4.5%"], [Savings Account - annualPercentageRate - "1.2%"].
answerCount: Relates a question to the total number of answers it has received. Also called "number of answers", "total replies", "answer tally". Examples: [Forum Question - answerCount - 5], [StackOverflow Post - answerCount - 12], [FAQ Question - answerCount - 1].
answerExplanation: Relates an answer to a step-by-step explanation, comment, or web content clarifying how the answer was reached. Also called "explanation of answer", "solution details", "answer rationale". Examples: [Math Answer - answerExplanation - Comment "First, isolate x by subtracting 5..."], [Coding Answer - answerExplanation - WebContent "This works because the API handles..."], [Trivia Answer - answerExplanation - Comment "The treaty was signed in 1919, ending..."].
antagonist: Relates a muscle to another muscle whose physical action counteracts or opposes it. Also called "opposing muscle", "counteracting muscle", "muscle antagonist". Examples: [Biceps Brachii - antagonist - Muscle "Triceps Brachii"], [Quadriceps - antagonist - Muscle "Hamstrings"], [Tibialis Anterior - antagonist - Muscle "Gastrocnemius"].
appearance: Relates a claim to a creative work in which that claim occurs or is mentioned. Also called "claim occurrence", "mentioned in", "found in". Examples: [Fact-Checked Claim - appearance - NewsArticle "Viral Facebook Post"], [Scientific Claim - appearance - ResearchPaper "Nature Journal Vol 5"], [Political Claim - appearance - VideoObject "Debate Broadcast"].
applicableCountry: Relates a merchant return policy to the country where the policy is valid or applies. Also called "return policy country", "valid country", "policy jurisdiction". Examples: [Return Policy - applicableCountry - "US"], [Refund Policy - applicableCountry - Country "Canada"], [Exchange Policy - applicableCountry - "DE"].
applicableLocation: Relates a drug cost or drug legal status to the administrative area or location where that cost or status applies. Also called "legal status location", "cost region", "applicable jurisdiction". Examples: [Cannabis Legal Status - applicableLocation - AdministrativeArea "California"], [Drug Cost Specification - applicableLocation - AdministrativeArea "United Kingdom"], [Prescription Status - applicableLocation - AdministrativeArea "Ontario"].
applicantLocationRequirements: Relates a job posting to the geographic locations or administrative areas from which applicants are allowed to apply. Also called "eligible applicant locations", "remote work locations", "geographic hiring requirements". Examples: [Remote Developer Job - applicantLocationRequirements - AdministrativeArea "United States"], [Writer Job - applicantLocationRequirements - AdministrativeArea "Canada"], [Designer Job - applicantLocationRequirements - AdministrativeArea "European Union"].
application: Relates an entry point to the software application that can complete the requested action. Also called "handling application", "executing software", "target app". Examples: [Search EntryPoint - application - "Google Search App"], [Play Music EntryPoint - application - "Spotify App"], [Open Document EntryPoint - application - "Adobe Acrobat"]. Distinct from actionApplication, which is a more specific sub-property.
applicationCategory: Relates a software application to its broad category or genre. Also called "app category", "software genre", "application type". Examples: [Angry Birds - applicationCategory - "Game"], [Photoshop - applicationCategory - "Multimedia"], [Slack - applicationCategory - "Communication"].
applicationContact: Relates a job posting to the contact point or details where applicants can seek further information. Also called "job contact", "hiring contact", "application inquiry point". Examples: [Developer Job - applicationContact - ContactPoint "hr@company.com"], [Manager Job - applicationContact - ContactPoint "Hiring Team Phone"], [Internship - applicationContact - ContactPoint "Recruiter Chat"].
applicationDeadline: Relates an educational or occupational program to the date or text indicating when it stops accepting applications. Also called "deadline date", "closing date for applications", "enrollment deadline". Examples: [MBA Program - applicationDeadline - "2024-01-15"], [Coding Bootcamp - applicationDeadline - "Rolling admissions"], [Nursing Course - applicationDeadline - "2023-11-30"].

confirmationNumber: An Invoice or Order has a Text value that confirms its receipt or payment. Also called "order confirmation", "payment confirmation", "booking reference". Examples: An order has confirmationNumber "ABC-12345". An invoice has confirmationNumber "INV-98765". An order has confirmationNumber "CONF-XYZ".
connectedTo: An AnatomicalStructure is connected to another AnatomicalStructure. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "attached to". Examples: The "Femur" is connectedTo "Tibia". The "Brain" is connectedTo "Spinal Cord". The "Heart" is connectedTo "Aorta".
constraintProperty: A ConstraintNode indicates a Property or URL used as a constraint, for example, in the definition of a StatisticalVariable. Also called "constrained by property", "limiting property", "restriction property". Examples: A constraint node has constraintProperty "schema:age". A constraint node has constraintProperty "dc:gender". A constraint node has constraintProperty "wikidata:P21".
contactOption: A ContactPoint specifies a ContactPointOption that is available on it (e.g., a toll-free number). Also called "contact feature", "communication option", "service option". Examples: A contact point has contactOption "TollFree". A contact point has contactOption "HearingImpairedSupported". A contact point has contactOption "Fax".
contactPoint: A HealthInsurancePlan, Organization, or Person has a ContactPoint for communication. Also called "contact information", "point of contact", "reach out to". Examples: An organization has contactPoint "Customer Service". A person has contactPoint "Email Address". A health insurance plan has contactPoint "Member Services".
contactPoints: An Organization or Person has a ContactPoint for communication. Also called "contact information", "points of contact", "communication channels". Examples: An organization has contactPoints "Customer Service". A person has contactPoints "Email Address". An organization has contactPoints "Phone Number".
contactType: A ContactPoint specifies Text describing its type, such as 'sales' or 'PR'. Also called "type of contact", "purpose of contact", "contact category". Examples: A contact point has contactType "Customer Service". A contact point has contactType "Technical Support". A contact point has contactType "Sales".
contactlessPayment: A PaymentCard specifies a Boolean indicating whether it supports a secure method for consumers to purchase products or services via RFID or NFC technology. Also called "tap to pay", "NFC payment", "RFID payment". Examples: A payment card has contactlessPayment "true". A payment card has contactlessPayment "false". A payment card has contactlessPayment "true".
containedIn: A Place is contained within another Place. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "Paris" is containedIn "France". "California" is containedIn "United States". "The Louvre" is containedIn "Paris".
containedInPlace: A Place is contained within another Place. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "Paris" is containedInPlace "France". "California" is containedInPlace "United States". "The Louvre" is containedInPlace "Paris".
containsPlace: A Place contains another Place. Also called "encompasses", "includes location", "holds place". Examples: "France" containsPlace "Paris". "United States" containsPlace "California". "Paris" containsPlace "The Louvre".
containsSeason: A RadioSeries, TVSeries, or VideoGameSeries contains a CreativeWorkSeason. Also called "has season", "includes season", "season part of series". Examples: A TV series has containsSeason "Season 1". A radio series has containsSeason "The Christmas Special". A video game series has containsSeason "Expansion Pack 1".
contentLocation: A CreativeWork depicts or describes a Place as its content location. Also called "setting", "location depicted", "place of content". Examples: A photograph has contentLocation "Eiffel Tower". A painting has contentLocation "Venice". A novel has contentLocation "London".
contentRating: A CreativeWork has a Rating or Text representing its official content rating. Also called "age rating", "movie rating", "TV rating". Examples: A movie has contentRating "MPAA PG-13". A video game has contentRating "ESRB M". A TV show has contentRating "TV-MA".
contentReferenceTime: A CreativeWork specifies a DateTime representing the specific time described by the work, especially for works emphasizing a particular moment within an Event. Also called "event time", "moment described", "time of content". Examples: An article has contentReferenceTime "2023-10-26T10:00:00Z". A video object has contentReferenceTime "2022-07-04T12:00:00Z". A news report has contentReferenceTime "2023-03-15T09:00:00Z".
contentSize: A MediaObject specifies Text representing its file size in (mega/kilo)bytes. Also called "file size", "media size", "data size". Examples: A media object has contentSize "10 MB". A media object has contentSize "2.5 GB". A media object has contentSize "500 KB".
contentType: An EntryPoint specifies the Text representing the supported content type(s) for its response. Also called "response type", "media type", "MIME type". Examples: An entry point has contentType "application/json". An entry point has contentType "text/html". An entry point has contentType "image/jpeg".
contentUrl: A MediaObject provides a URL to the actual bytes of the media object, such as an image file or video file. Also called "media URL", "file URL", "download link". Examples: An image object has contentUrl "https://example.com/image.jpg". A video object has contentUrl "https://example.com/video.mp4". An audio object has contentUrl "https://example.com/audio.mp3".
contraindication: A MedicalDevice or MedicalTherapy has a MedicalContraindication or Text describing a contraindication for its use. Also called "contraindicated for", "not recommended for", "warning against". Examples: A medical therapy has contraindication "Pregnancy". A medical device has contraindication "Patients with pacemakers". A medical therapy has contraindication "Allergy to penicillin".
contributor: A CreativeWork or Event has an Organization or Person who is a secondary contributor. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: An article has contributor "Jane Doe". A conference has contributor "Acme Corp". A book has contributor "Editor Name".
cookTime: A Recipe specifies a Duration representing the time it takes to actually cook the dish, in ISO 8601 duration format. Also called "cooking duration", "active cooking time", "preparation time". Examples: A recipe has cookTime "PT30M" (30 minutes). A recipe has cookTime "PT2H" (2 hours). A recipe has cookTime "PT1H15M" (1 hour 15 minutes).
cookingMethod: A Recipe specifies Text describing the method of cooking, such as Frying or Steaming. Also called "preparation method", "culinary technique", "cooking style". Examples: A recipe has cookingMethod "Frying". A recipe has cookingMethod "Baking". A recipe has cookingMethod "Steaming".
copyrightHolder: A CreativeWork has a copyrightHolder, which is the Organization or Person that legally owns its copyright. Also called copyright owned by, legal owner of copyright, copyright held by. Examples: "The Lord of the Rings" copyrightHolder J.R.R. Tolkien Estate, "Mona Lisa" copyrightHolder French State, "Star Wars: A New Hope" copyrightHolder Lucasfilm.
copyrightNotice: A CreativeWork has a copyrightNotice, which is the textual statement describing its copyright aspects. Also called copyright statement, copyright declaration, copyright text. Examples: "My Novel" copyrightNotice "© 2023 John Doe. All rights reserved.", "Company Website" copyrightNotice "Copyright © 2023 Example Corp.", "Academic Paper" copyrightNotice "Published by IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted." Distinct from copyrightHolder, which identifies the entity owning the copyright, whereas copyrightNotice is the descriptive text.
copyrightYear: A CreativeWork has a copyrightYear, which is the year its copyright was first asserted. Also called year of copyright, first copyright year, copyright date. Examples: "Classic Album" copyrightYear 1973, "New Software" copyrightYear 2024, "Historical Document" copyrightYear 1888. Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first publication, whereas copyrightYear is specifically the year the copyright was claimed.
correction: A CreativeWork has a correction, which indicates a change or amendment to its content. Also called content correction, work amendment, revision. Examples: "News Article" correction "Typo in headline corrected.", "Research Paper" correction "Updated data in Table 2.", "Book Edition" correction "Minor factual errors addressed."
correctionsPolicy: An Organization (e.g., NewsMediaOrganization) has a correctionsPolicy, which is a statement describing its disclosure and correction policy for errors. Also called error policy, editorial policy, revision guidelines. Examples: "The New York Times" correctionsPolicy "Our policy on corrections and clarifications.", "Academic Journal" correctionsPolicy "Guidelines for submitting corrections.", "Tech Company" correctionsPolicy "How we handle product error reports."
costCategory: A DrugCost has a costCategory, which specifies the type of cost, such as wholesale or retail. Also called cost type, price category, expense classification. Examples: "Insulin" costCategory "Wholesale", "Antibiotic" costCategory "Retail", "Vaccine" costCategory "Reimbursement Cap".
costCurrency: A DrugCost has a costCurrency, which specifies the 3-letter ISO 4217 code for the currency of the drug cost. Also called currency unit, price currency, monetary unit. Examples: "Pain Reliever" costCurrency "USD", "Antihistamine" costCurrency "EUR", "Vitamin Supplement" costCurrency "JPY".
costOrigin: A DrugCost has a costOrigin, which provides additional details about the source of the cost data. Also called cost source, pricing origin, data source. Examples: "Generic Drug" costOrigin "Medicare Part B", "Specialty Medication" costOrigin "Manufacturer's List Price", "Over-the-counter" costOrigin "Pharmacy Survey Data".
costPerUnit: A DrugCost has a costPerUnit, which specifies the cost for a single unit of the drug. Also called unit price, price per item, cost rate. Examples: "Pill Bottle" costPerUnit 0.50, "Injection Vial" costPerUnit 12.99, "Cream Tube" costPerUnit "$5.99 per 100g".
countriesNotSupported: A SoftwareApplication has countriesNotSupported, which lists the countries where the application is not available or functional. Also called unsupported regions, restricted countries, unavailable in. Examples: "Streaming App" countriesNotSupported "CN, RU", "Gaming Software" countriesNotSupported "Cuba, Iran", "Productivity Tool" countriesNotSupported "North Korea". Distinct from countriesSupported, which lists the countries where the application is available.
countriesSupported: A SoftwareApplication has countriesSupported, which lists the countries where the application is available or functional. Also called supported regions, available in, operational in. Examples: "Mobile Game" countriesSupported "US, CA, MX", "Business Software" countriesSupported "Germany, France, UK", "Social Media App" countriesSupported "Worldwide (excluding China)". Distinct from countriesNotSupported, which lists the countries where the application is unavailable.
countryOfAssembly: A Product has a countryOfAssembly, which specifies the place where the product was put together. Also called assembled in, manufacturing location, assembly country. Examples: "Smartphone" countryOfAssembly "Vietnam", "Automobile" countryOfAssembly "Mexico", "Furniture" countryOfAssembly "Poland". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which is the general country of origin, and countryOfLastProcessing, which is where it was last processed before import.
countryOfLastProcessing: A Product has a countryOfLastProcessing, which specifies the place where the item was last processed and tested before importation. Also called last processed in, pre-import processing country, final testing location. Examples: "Electronic Component" countryOfLastProcessing "Malaysia", "Textile Product" countryOfLastProcessing "Bangladesh", "Food Item" countryOfLastProcessing "Netherlands". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which is the general country of origin, and countryOfAssembly, which is where it was assembled.
countryOfOrigin: A CreativeWork or Product has a countryOfOrigin, which specifies the country from which it originates. Also called origin country, nation of origin, produced in. Examples: "French Wine" countryOfOrigin "France", "Japanese Anime" countryOfOrigin "Japan", "German Car" countryOfOrigin "Germany". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where a product was assembled, and countryOfLastProcessing, which indicates where it was last processed before import.
course: An ExerciseAction has a course, which is the physical location where the action was taken. Also called exercise location, training ground, route. Examples: "Morning Run" course "Central Park Loop", "Golf Game" course "Augusta National", "Cycling Race" course "Tour de France Route". Distinct from courseCode, courseMode, coursePrerequisites, courseSchedule, and courseWorkload, which refer to aspects of an educational course, whereas this property refers to a physical location for an exercise action.
courseCode: A Course has a courseCode, which is the identifier used by the course provider. Also called course ID, subject code, catalog number. Examples: "Introduction to Programming" courseCode "CS101", "Calculus I" courseCode "MA101", "Art History" courseCode "AH205". Distinct from course, which refers to a physical location for an exercise action, whereas courseCode identifies an educational course.
courseMode: A CourseInstance has a courseMode, which describes the medium or means of delivery or the mode of study. Also called delivery method, study mode, learning format. Examples: "Online Course" courseMode "online", "Evening Class" courseMode "onsite", "Blended Learning Program" courseMode "blended".
coursePrerequisites: A Course has coursePrerequisites, which are the requirements for taking the course. Also called course requirements, entry criteria, prior knowledge. Examples: "Advanced Physics" coursePrerequisites "Calculus I", "Programming II" coursePrerequisites "CS101", "Graduate Seminar" coursePrerequisites "Permission of instructor".
courseSchedule: A CourseInstance has a courseSchedule, which represents the length and pace of the course. Also called class schedule, course timetable, study plan. Examples: "Fall Semester Course" courseSchedule "Mondays and Wednesdays, 9-11 AM", "Intensive Workshop" courseSchedule "Full-time for 3 weeks", "Online Module" courseSchedule "Self-paced over 8 weeks".
courseWorkload: A CourseInstance has a courseWorkload, which describes the amount of work expected of students. Also called student effort, study hours, expected commitment. Examples: "Introductory Course" courseWorkload "3 hours lecture, 2 hours lab, 5 hours independent study per week", "Project-based Class" courseWorkload "10-15 hours per week", "Summer Session" courseWorkload "20 hours per week".
coverageEndTime: A LiveBlogPosting has a coverageEndTime, which is the time when the live blog will stop covering an Event. Also called live blog end time, event coverage conclusion, reporting end. Examples: "Election Night Blog" coverageEndTime "2024-11-06T03:00:00Z", "Sports Match Live Feed" coverageEndTime "2023-10-27T19:30:00Z", "Conference Updates" coverageEndTime "2024-05-15T17:00:00Z". Distinct from dateModified, which is when the blog post itself was last changed, whereas coverageEndTime is about the event coverage.
coverageStartTime: A LiveBlogPosting has a coverageStartTime, which is the time when the live blog will begin covering an Event. Also called live blog start time, event coverage beginning, reporting start. Examples: "Election Night Blog" coverageStartTime "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Match Live Feed" coverageStartTime "2023-10-27T16:00:00Z", "Conference Updates" coverageStartTime "2024-05-15T09:00:00Z". Distinct from dateCreated, which is when the blog post was created, whereas coverageStartTime is about the event coverage.
creativeWorkStatus: A CreativeWork has a creativeWorkStatus, which indicates its stage in a lifecycle. Also called work status, publication stage, lifecycle status. Examples: "Novel Draft" creativeWorkStatus "Draft", "Software Project" creativeWorkStatus "Incomplete", "Archived Document" creativeWorkStatus "Obsolete".
creator: A CreativeWork or UserComments has a creator, which is the Organization or Person responsible for its creation. Also called author, originator, maker. Examples: "Painting" creator "Leonardo da Vinci", "Website" creator "Google", "Comment" creator "Jane Doe".
credentialCategory: A Credential has a credentialCategory, which specifies the type or category of the credential. Also called credential type, certification category, badge type. Examples: "Bachelor's Degree" credentialCategory "degree", "Project Management Professional" credentialCategory "certificate", "Open Badge" credentialCategory "badge".
creditText: A CreativeWork has a creditText, which is text used to credit person(s) and/or organization(s) associated with it. Also called attribution text, acknowledgment, credit line. Examples: "Movie" creditText "Directed by Christopher Nolan", "Song" creditText "Lyrics by Bob Dylan", "Photograph" creditText "Photo by Annie Leibovitz".
creditedTo: A MusicRelease has creditedTo, which is the group the release is credited to, if different from the byArtist. Also called release attribution, credited artist, album credit. Examples: "Album X" creditedTo "The Band (featuring Guest Artist)", "Single Y" creditedTo "Project Z", "Soundtrack" creditedTo "Various Artists". Distinct from creator, which is a general property for the entity responsible for a CreativeWork, whereas creditedTo is specific to music releases and their attribution.
cssSelector: A SpeakableSpecification or WebPageElement has a cssSelector, which is a CSS selector string used to identify it. Also called CSS path, selector string, element selector. Examples: "Main Content" cssSelector "#main-content", "Article Title" cssSelector ".article-title", "Navigation Menu" cssSelector "nav ul li a".
currenciesAccepted: A LocalBusiness has currenciesAccepted, which specifies the currencies it accepts for payment. Also called accepted currency, payment currency, tender. Examples: "Coffee Shop" currenciesAccepted "USD, EUR", "Online Store" currenciesAccepted "USD, BTC", "Local Market" currenciesAccepted "Ithaca HOUR". Distinct from currency, which specifies the currency of a specific monetary amount, whereas currenciesAccepted lists what a business takes.
currency: A MonetaryAmount or related specification has a currency, which specifies the 3-letter ISO 4217 code for the currency in which the amount is expressed. Also called monetary unit, unit of currency, denomination. Examples: "Price" currency "USD", "Loan Amount" currency "EUR", "Exchange Rate" currency "JPY". Distinct from currenciesAccepted, which lists the currencies a business accepts, whereas currency specifies the unit of a particular monetary value.
currentExchangeRate: An ExchangeRateSpecification has a currentExchangeRate, which specifies the current price of a currency. Also called exchange value, conversion rate, prevailing rate. Examples: "USD to EUR" currentExchangeRate "0.92", "GBP to JPY" currentExchangeRate "185.50", "BTC to USD" currentExchangeRate "65000".
customer: An Invoice or Order has a customer, which is the Organization or Person placing the order or paying the invoice. Also called client, buyer, recipient. Examples: "Online Order" customer "Alice Smith", "Business Invoice" customer "Acme Corp.", "Service Agreement" customer "John Doe".
customerRemorseReturnFees: A MerchantReturnPolicy has customerRemorseReturnFees, which specifies the type of return fees if a product is returned due to customer remorse. Also called remorse return charges, change-of-mind fees, regret return costs. Examples: "Electronics Store" customerRemorseReturnFees "ReturnShippingFees", "Clothing Retailer" customerRemorseReturnFees "NoFees", "Furniture Shop" customerRemorseReturnFees "RestockingFee".
customerRemorseReturnLabelSource: A MerchantReturnPolicy has customerRemorseReturnLabelSource, which specifies how the customer obtains a return shipping label for a product returned due to remorse. Also called remorse return label method, label provision, shipping label source. Examples: "Online Retailer" customerRemorseReturnLabelSource "DownloadAndPrint", "Department Store" customerRemorseReturnLabelSource "InStore", "Specialty Shop" customerRemorseReturnLabelSource "ShipperSupplied".
customerRemorseReturnShippingFeesAmount: A MerchantReturnPolicy has customerRemorseReturnShippingFeesAmount, which specifies the amount of shipping costs if a product is returned due to customer remorse. Also called remorse return shipping cost, regret shipping fee, return postage amount. Examples: "Online Purchase" customerRemorseReturnShippingFeesAmount "$5.00", "Apparel Order" customerRemorseReturnShippingFeesAmount "0", "Large Item" customerRemorseReturnShippingFeesAmount "$25.00".
cutoffTime: A ServicePeriod or ShippingDeliveryTime has a cutoffTime, which is the time after which orders received on that day will be processed the next day. Also called order cutoff, daily processing limit, last order time. Examples: "Same-day Delivery" cutoffTime "15:00:00-05:00", "Next-day Shipping" cutoffTime "17:00:00Z", "Warehouse Pickup" cutoffTime "18:30:00".
cvdCollectionDate: A CDCPMDRecord has a cvdCollectionDate, which is the date for which patient counts are reported. Also called data collection date, report date, patient count date. Examples: "Hospital Data" cvdCollectionDate "2023-01-15", "Facility Report" cvdCollectionDate "2023-02-01T10:00:00Z", "Daily Update" cvdCollectionDate "2023-03-10".
cvdFacilityCounty: A CDCPMDRecord has a cvdFacilityCounty, which is the name of the county of the NHSN facility to which the data record applies. Also called facility county, hospital county, reporting county. Examples: "COVID-19 Data" cvdFacilityCounty "Los Angeles County", "NHSN Report" cvdFacilityCounty "Cook County", "Healthcare Record" cvdFacilityCounty "King County".
cvdFacilityId: A CDCPMDRecord has a cvdFacilityId, which is the identifier of the NHSN facility to which the data record applies. Also called facility ID, hospital identifier, NHSN ID. Examples: "COVID-19 Data" cvdFacilityId "12345", "NHSN Report" cvdFacilityId "67890", "Healthcare Record" cvdFacilityId "ABCDE".
cvdNumBeds: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumBeds, which is the total number of hospital inpatient beds, including staffed, licensed, and overflow beds. Also called total inpatient beds, hospital bed count, available beds. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumBeds 250, "Facility B" cvdNumBeds 100, "Medical Center" cvdNumBeds 500.
cvdNumBedsOcc: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumBedsOcc, which is the total number of staffed inpatient beds that are currently occupied. Also called occupied inpatient beds, bed occupancy, current bed usage. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumBedsOcc 200, "Facility B" cvdNumBedsOcc 80, "Medical Center" cvdNumBedsOcc 450.
cvdNumC19Died: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumC19Died, which is the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who died in the hospital, ED, or any overflow location. Also called COVID-19 deaths, virus fatalities, pandemic deaths. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumC19Died 5, "Facility B" cvdNumC19Died 1, "Medical Center" cvdNumC19Died 12.
cvdNumC19HOPats: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumC19HOPats, which is the number of patients hospitalized with onset of suspected or confirmed COVID-19 14 or more days after hospitalization. Also called hospital-onset COVID-19 patients, nosocomial COVID-19, late-onset cases. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumC19HOPats 2, "Facility B" cvdNumC19HOPats 0, "Medical Center" cvdNumC19HOPats 3.
cvdNumC19HospPats: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumC19HospPats, which is the number of patients currently hospitalized with suspected or confirmed COVID-19. Also called hospitalized COVID-19 patients, current COVID-19 admissions, virus inpatients. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumC19HospPats 30, "Facility B" cvdNumC19HospPats 10, "Medical Center" cvdNumC19HospPats 75.
cvdNumC19MechVentPats: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumC19MechVentPats, which is the number of hospitalized patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who are on a mechanical ventilator. Also called COVID-19 ventilated patients, virus patients on ventilators, ICU COVID-19 ventilated. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumC19MechVentPats 8, "Facility B" cvdNumC19MechVentPats 3, "Medical Center" cvdNumC19MechVentPats 20.
cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats, which is the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 in the ED or overflow awaiting an inpatient bed and on a mechanical ventilator. Also called ED/overflow ventilated COVID-19, emergency ventilated virus patients, surge ventilated. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats 2, "Facility B" cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats 1, "Medical Center" cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats 5.
cvdNumC19OverflowPats: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumC19OverflowPats, which is the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 in the ED or any overflow location awaiting an inpatient bed. Also called ED/overflow COVID-19 patients, emergency virus patients, surge capacity patients. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumC19OverflowPats 15, "Facility B" cvdNumC19OverflowPats 5, "Medical Center" cvdNumC19OverflowPats 30.
cvdNumICUBeds: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumICUBeds, which is the total number of staffed inpatient intensive care unit (ICU) beds. Also called total ICU beds, critical care beds, intensive care capacity. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumICUBeds 20, "Facility B" cvdNumICUBeds 8, "Medical Center" cvdNumICUBeds 40.
cvdNumICUBedsOcc: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumICUBedsOcc, which is the total number of staffed inpatient ICU beds that are currently occupied. Also called occupied ICU beds, ICU bed occupancy, critical care bed usage. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumICUBedsOcc 18, "Facility B" cvdNumICUBedsOcc 7, "Medical Center" cvdNumICUBedsOcc 35.
cvdNumTotBeds: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumTotBeds, which is the total number of all inpatient and outpatient beds, including all staffed, ICU, licensed, and overflow beds. Also called total hospital beds, overall bed count, comprehensive bed capacity. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumTotBeds 300, "Facility B" cvdNumTotBeds 120, "Medical Center" cvdNumTotBeds 600.
cvdNumVent: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumVent, which is the total number of mechanical ventilators available. Also called total ventilators, ventilator count, available breathing machines. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumVent 50, "Facility B" cvdNumVent 20, "Medical Center" cvdNumVent 100.
cvdNumVentUse: A CDCPMDRecord has cvdNumVentUse, which is the total number of mechanical ventilators currently in use. Also called ventilators in use, occupied ventilators, breathing machines in use. Examples: "Hospital A" cvdNumVentUse 30, "Facility B" cvdNumVentUse 15, "Medical Center" cvdNumVentUse 70.
data: An InstantaneousEvent has data, which is information associated with the event. Also called event data, associated information, log message. Examples: "Sensor Reading" data "Temperature: 25C", "System Alert" data "Error code 404", "User Action" data "Login successful".
dataFeedElement: A DataFeed has a dataFeedElement, which is an item contained within the feed. Also called feed item, data entry, feed content. Examples: "News Feed" dataFeedElement "Latest Article", "Product Catalog" dataFeedElement "New Product Listing", "Event Stream" dataFeedElement "Upcoming Event".
dataset: A DataCatalog has a dataset, which is a collection of data contained within the catalog. Also called cataloged dataset, data collection, data entry. Examples: "Government Data Portal" dataset "Census 2020 Data", "Research Repository" dataset "Climate Change Projections", "Open Data Catalog" dataset "Traffic Flow Statistics".
datasetTimeInterval: A Dataset has a datasetTimeInterval, which specifies the range of temporal applicability of the dataset. Also called temporal coverage, data period, time span. Examples: "Census Data" datasetTimeInterval "2011", "Historical Weather Records" datasetTimeInterval "1900-2000", "Economic Survey" datasetTimeInterval "2020-01-01/2020-12-31".
dateCreated: A CreativeWork or DataFeedItem has a dateCreated, which is the date on which it was initially made or added. Also called creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Photograph" dateCreated "2023-03-15", "Software Project" dateCreated "2022-01-01", "Blog Post" dateCreated "2024-01-20T10:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release, and dateModified, which is the date of the most recent change.
dateDeleted: A DataFeedItem has a dateDeleted, which is the datetime the item was removed from the DataFeed. Also called removal date, deletion timestamp, item removed. Examples: "Old Product Listing" dateDeleted "2023-11-01T14:30:00Z", "Archived Article" dateDeleted "2024-02-29", "Expired Event" dateDeleted "2023-07-01".
dateIssued: A Ticket has a dateIssued, which is the date when the ticket was generated or provided. Also called issue date, ticket date, date of issuance. Examples: "Concert Ticket" dateIssued "2024-04-01", "Flight Ticket" dateIssued "2023-12-20T10:00:00Z", "Parking Permit" dateIssued "2024-01-01".
dateModified: A CreativeWork or DataFeedItem has a dateModified, which is the date on which it was most recently changed or updated. Also called last modified date, update date, revision date. Examples: "Wikipedia Article" dateModified "2024-05-01T12:00:00Z", "Software Documentation" dateModified "2023-10-25", "Data Record" dateModified "2024-01-15". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the initial creation date, and datePublished, which is the date of first public release.
datePosted: A JobPosting, RealEstateListing, or SpecialAnnouncement has a datePosted, which is the publication date of the online listing. Also called posting date, listing date, announcement date. Examples: "Job Opening" datePosted "2024-05-01", "Apartment for Rent" datePosted "2024-04-20", "Public Notice" datePosted "2023-11-10T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is for general publication or broadcast, whereas datePosted is specifically for online listings.
datePublished: A CreativeWork or Certification has a datePublished, which is the date of its first public release or broadcast. Also called publication date, release date, broadcast date. Examples: "Book" datePublished "1984-06-08", "News Report" datePublished "2024-05-02T08:00:00Z", "Certification" datePublished "2023-09-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is when the work was initially made, and datePosted, which is for online listings rather than general publication.
dateRead: A Message has a dateRead, which is the date and time at which the message was read by the recipient. Also called read timestamp, message opened, viewed date. Examples: "Email" dateRead "2024-05-02T10:30:00Z", "Chat Message" dateRead "2024-05-02T10:35:15Z", "Notification" dateRead "2024-05-02T10:40:00Z".
dateReceived: A Message has a dateReceived, which is the date and time the message was delivered to the recipient. Also called reception date, delivery timestamp, message arrived. Examples: "Email" dateReceived "2024-05-02T10:29:00Z", "Chat Message" dateReceived "2024-05-02T10:35:00Z", "Notification" dateReceived "2024-05-02T10:39:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched by the sender.
dateSent: A Message has a dateSent, which is the date and time at which the message was dispatched by the sender. Also called dispatch date, transmission date, message sent. Examples: "The incentive is eligibleWithSupplier 'Utility Company A'", "The rebate is eligibleWithSupplier 'Retailer X'", "This offer is eligibleWithSupplier 'Contractor Y'".
email: A ContactPoint, Organization, or Person has an email address. Also called "email address", "contact email". Examples: "The organization's email is 'info@example.com'", "The person's email is 'john.doe@email.com'", "The contact point has email 'support@service.com'".
embedUrl: A MediaObject has an embed URL, which is a URL pointing to a player for the specific video or media. Also called "player URL", "iframe src". Examples: "The video has embedUrl 'https://www.youtube.com/embed/videoid'", "The media object's embedUrl is 'https://player.vimeo.com/video/12345'", "The content provides an embedUrl for its player.".
embeddedTextCaption: An AudioObject, ImageObject, or VideoObject has an embedded text caption, which represents textual captioning from the media object. Also called "media caption", "text overlay". Examples: "The image has embeddedTextCaption 'Funny meme text'", "The video includes embeddedTextCaption for a scene", "The audio object contains embeddedTextCaption for spoken words.".
emissionsCO2: A Vehicle has CO2 emissions, which is the amount of carbon dioxide emitted in grams per kilometer. Also called "carbon emissions", "CO2 output". Examples: "The car has emissionsCO2 '120 g/km'", "The vehicle's emissionsCO2 is '95'", "This model has low emissionsCO2.".
employee: An Organization has an employee, who is a person working for that organization. Also called "staff member", "worker". Examples: "The company has employee 'Jane Doe'", "The organization lists 'John Smith' as an employee", "'Alice Brown' is an employee of the firm.".
employees: An Organization has employees, who are people working for that organization. Also called "staff", "workforce". Examples: "The company has employees 'Jane Doe' and 'John Smith'", "The organization lists its employees", "The firm's employees are dedicated.". Distinct from employee, which typically refers to a single person.
employerOverview: A JobPosting includes an employer overview, which is a description of the employer, career opportunities, and work environment. Also called "company profile", "about the employer". Examples: "The job posting provides an employerOverview of the company culture", "The listing includes an employerOverview detailing career growth", "The employerOverview describes the work environment.".
employmentType: A JobPosting specifies an employment type, which describes the nature of the employment. Also called "job type", "work arrangement". Examples: "The job posting has employmentType 'full-time'", "The position is employmentType 'part-time'", "This role is employmentType 'contract'".
employmentUnit: A JobPosting specifies an employment unit, which indicates the department, unit, or facility where the job is to be performed. Also called "department", "work unit", "reporting facility". Examples: "The job is in employmentUnit 'Marketing Department'", "The position's employmentUnit is 'Headquarters'", "The role is within employmentUnit 'Research & Development'".
encodesBioChemEntity: A Gene encodes a BioChemEntity, meaning this gene provides the instructions for producing that biochemical entity. Also called "produces", "codes for". Examples: "The gene encodesBioChemEntity 'protein X'", "This gene encodesBioChemEntity 'RNA molecule'", "The DNA sequence encodesBioChemEntity 'enzyme Y'".
encodesCreativeWork: A MediaObject encodes a CreativeWork, meaning the media object is a digital representation or version of that creative work. Also called "represents", "is a version of". Examples: "The video file encodesCreativeWork 'Movie Title'", "The audio recording encodesCreativeWork 'Song Name'", "The image encodesCreativeWork 'Artwork Piece'".
encoding: A CreativeWork has an encoding, which is a media object that represents or encodes the creative work. Also called "media representation", "digital version". Examples: "The CreativeWork has an encoding as an MP4 file", "The book's encoding is an e-book file", "The artwork has an encoding as a high-resolution image.".
encodingFormat: A CreativeWork or MediaObject specifies an encoding format, which is the media type typically expressed using a MIME format. Also called "file format", "media type". Examples: "The video has encodingFormat 'video/mp4'", "The CreativeWork's encodingFormat is 'application/pdf'", "The image uses encodingFormat 'image/jpeg'".
encodingType: An EntryPoint specifies an encoding type, which is the supported encoding type(s) for a request to that entry point. Also called "request encoding", "data encoding". Examples: "The entry point supports encodingType 'application/json'", "The API endpoint has encodingType 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'", "This service accepts encodingType 'text/xml'".
encodings: A CreativeWork has encodings, which are media objects that represent or encode the creative work. Also called "media representations", "digital versions". Examples: "The CreativeWork has encodings as MP4 and WebM files", "The book's encodings include e-book and audiobook formats", "The artwork has encodings as various image resolutions.".
endDate: A CreativeWorkSeason, CreativeWorkSeries, DatedMoneySpecification, EducationalOccupationalProgram, Event, MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride, Role, or Schedule has an end date, which is the date and time when the item concludes. Also called "completion date", "finish date". Examples: "The event's endDate is '2024-12-31'", "The season has an endDate of '2025-03-15'", "The program's endDate is '2024-06-30T17:00:00'".
endOffset: A Clip has an end offset, which is the end time of the clip expressed as the number of seconds from the beginning of the work. Also called "clip end time", "segment end". Examples: "The clip has an endOffset of '120' seconds", "The video segment's endOffset is '300'", "The audio clip ends at endOffset '60'".
endTime: An Action, FoodEstablishmentReservation, InteractionCounter, MediaObject, or Schedule has an end time, which is the time when something is expected to conclude or was performed. Also called "completion time", "finish time". Examples: "The reservation's endTime is '20:00'", "The action was performed until endTime '2024-07-20T18:30:00'", "The media clip ends at endTime '00:01:30'". Distinct from endDate, which is used for events and spans a full date.
endorsee: An EndorseAction has an endorsee, who is the person or organization being supported by the action. Also called "supported party", "beneficiary". Examples: "The action's endorsee is 'Candidate A'", "The endorsement is for endorsee 'Organization X'", "The campaign supports endorsee 'Jane Doe'".
endorsers: A Diet has endorsers, who are people or organizations that support the plan. Also called "supporters", "advocates". Examples: "The diet has endorsers 'Dr. Smith' and 'Nutritionist Jane'", "The plan lists several endorsers", "The program's endorsers include medical professionals.".
energyEfficiencyScaleMax: EnergyConsumptionDetails specify the maximum energy efficiency class on the regulated EU scale for a product category. Also called "highest efficiency class", "best energy rating". Examples: "The product's energyEfficiencyScaleMax is 'A+++'", "The details indicate energyEfficiencyScaleMax 'A'", "The scale goes up to energyEfficiencyScaleMax 'B'".
energyEfficiencyScaleMin: EnergyConsumptionDetails specify the minimum energy efficiency class on the regulated EU scale for a product category. Also called "lowest efficiency class", "worst energy rating". Examples: "The product's energyEfficiencyScaleMin is 'D'", "The details indicate energyEfficiencyScaleMin 'G'", "The scale starts at energyEfficiencyScaleMin 'C'".
engineDisplacement: An EngineSpecification specifies the engine displacement, which is the total volume swept by all pistons in an internal combustion engine. Also called "engine volume", "cylinder volume". Examples: "The engine has engineDisplacement '2.0 LTR'", "The specification lists engineDisplacement '1998 CMQ'", "The vehicle features engineDisplacement '122 INQ'".
enginePower: An EngineSpecification specifies the engine power, which is the power output of the vehicle's engine. Also called "horsepower", "engine output", "kilowatt rating". Examples: "The engine has enginePower '150 BHP'", "The specification lists enginePower '110 KWT'", "The vehicle features enginePower '180 PS'".
engineType: An EngineSpecification specifies the engine type, which is the kind of engine powering the vehicle. Also called "motor type", "powerplant type". Examples: "The engine specification lists engineType 'petrol'", "The vehicle has engineType 'electric'", "This model features engineType 'hybrid'".
entertainmentBusiness: A PerformAction occurs at an entertainment business, which is the venue where the action took place. Also called "performance venue", "show location". Examples: "The action occurred at entertainmentBusiness 'Concert Hall'", "The play was performed at entertainmentBusiness 'Local Theater'", "The event took place at entertainmentBusiness 'Comedy Club'".
epidemiology: A MedicalCondition or PhysicalActivity describes its epidemiology, which refers to the characteristics of associated patients. Also called "disease demographics", "patient characteristics". Examples: "The condition's epidemiology shows higher incidence in older adults", "The physical activity's epidemiology relates to age and gender", "The study details the epidemiology of the disease.".
episode: A CreativeWorkSeason, RadioSeries, TVSeries, or VideoGameSeries includes an episode, which is a single installment within the series or season. Also called "series episode", "season episode". Examples: "The TV series includes episode 'Pilot'", "The season has episode 'Episode 3'", "The video game series features episode 'Chapter 1'".
episodeNumber: An Episode has an episode number, which is its position within an ordered group of episodes. Also called "episode index", "sequence number". Examples: "The episode has episodeNumber '1'", "The installment's episodeNumber is '10'", "This is episodeNumber '5' of the season.".
episodes: A CreativeWorkSeason, RadioSeries, TVSeries, or VideoGameSeries includes episodes, which are installments within the series or season. Also called "series installments", "season episodes". Examples: "The TV series includes episodes 'Pilot' and 'Finale'", "The season has several episodes", "The video game series features multiple episodes.".
equal: A QualitativeValue is equal to another QualitativeValue, indicating that the subject has the same qualitative measure as the object. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as". Examples: "'High' is equal to 'Very High' in some contexts", "The value 'Good' is equal to 'Excellent' for this metric", "This qualitative value is equal to that one.".
error: An Action has an error, which provides more information on the cause of a failure. Also called "failure reason", "problem details". Examples: "The action resulted in an error 'Invalid Input'", "The process encountered an error object", "The system reported an error during execution.".
errorCode: An Error has an error code, which is an application or platform-dependent code indicating the specific type of error. Also called "error identifier", "status code". Examples: "The error has errorCode '404'", "The system reported errorCode 'AUTH_FAILED'", "The problem is identified by errorCode '1001'".
estimatedCost: A HowTo or HowToSupply has an estimated cost, which is the approximate cost of the supplies consumed when performing instructions. Also called "approximate cost", "projected expense". Examples: "The how-to guide lists estimatedCost '50 USD'", "The supply has an estimatedCost of '10-20 EUR'", "The instructions include an estimatedCost for materials.".
estimatedFlightDuration: A Flight has an estimated flight duration, which is the approximate time the flight will take. Also called "flight time", "approximate duration". Examples: "The flight has estimatedFlightDuration 'PT2H30M'", "The journey's estimatedFlightDuration is '4 hours'", "The plane trip has an estimatedFlightDuration of 'P0DT05H00M'".
estimatedSalary: A JobPosting or Occupation has an estimated salary, which is an approximate salary based on various factors. Also called "projected salary", "average pay". Examples: "The job posting lists estimatedSalary '50000-70000 USD'", "The occupation has an estimatedSalary as a MonetaryAmountDistribution", "The role offers an estimatedSalary of '60000'".
estimatesRiskOf: A MedicalRiskEstimator estimates the risk of a MedicalEntity, which is the condition, complication, or symptom whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses risk of". Examples: "The estimator estimatesRiskOf 'heart disease'", "The tool estimatesRiskOf 'stroke'", "This model estimatesRiskOf 'diabetes complications'".
ethicsPolicy: An Organization or NewsMediaOrganization has an ethics policy, which is a statement about its ethical standards and practices. Also called "code of ethics", "conduct policy". Examples: "The news organization published its ethicsPolicy", "The company's ethicsPolicy covers journalistic practices", "The organization's ethicsPolicy outlines its values.".
event: An InformAction, InviteAction, JoinAction, LeaveAction, Organization, Place, or PlayAction is associated with an event, which is an upcoming or past occurrence. Also called "associated event", "related event". Examples: "The organization is hosting an event 'Annual Conference'", "The place is known for its event 'Summer Festival'", "The action relates to event 'Birthday Party'".
eventAttendanceMode: An Event has an event attendance mode, which indicates whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance type", "event format".
