Examples: "The event has eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "The conference's eventAttendanceMode is 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'", "This gathering has eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'".
eventSchedule: An Event has an event schedule, which associates it with a schedule for a series of repeating events. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable". Examples: "The event has an eventSchedule for weekly classes", "The program's eventSchedule details its recurring sessions", "This event is part of an eventSchedule.". Distinct from startDate/endDate, which are defined within the schedule itself.
eventStatus: An Event has an event status, which represents its current status, such as cancelled or rescheduled. Also called "event state", "status of event". Examples: "The event has eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "The concert's eventStatus is 'EventRescheduled'", "This gathering has eventStatus 'EventScheduled'".
events: An Organization or Place is associated with events, which are upcoming or past occurrences. Also called "associated events", "related events". Examples: "The organization is hosting several events", "The place is known for its events", "The venue's events calendar is full.". Distinct from event, which typically refers to a single event.
evidenceLevel: A MedicalGuideline has an evidenceLevel that indicates the strength of the data used to formulate it. Also called "strength of evidence", "data reliability", "guideline evidence strength". Examples: "A guideline has an evidenceLevel of 'Strong'.", "The medical guideline's evidenceLevel is 'Moderate'.", "This guideline's evidenceLevel is 'Weak'."
evidenceOrigin: A MedicalGuideline has an evidenceOrigin that describes the source of the data used to formulate the guidance. Also called "data source", "guideline data origin", "source of evidence". Examples: "The guideline's evidenceOrigin is 'Randomized Controlled Trial'.", "This guideline has an evidenceOrigin of 'Consensus Opinion'.", "The evidenceOrigin for the guidance was 'Systematic Review'."
exampleOfWork: A CreativeWork is an exampleOfWork of another CreativeWork if it is an instance, realization, or derivation of that work. Also called "instance of", "realization of", "derivation of", "based on". Examples: "A specific painting is an exampleOfWork of a general artistic style.", "A movie adaptation is an exampleOfWork of the original novel.", "A particular performance is an exampleOfWork of a musical composition."
exceptDate: A Schedule has an exceptDate that specifies a Date or DateTime when a scheduled Event will not occur. Also called "excluded date", "cancellation date", "unscheduled date", "date of exception". Examples: "The class schedule has an exceptDate of '2023-12-25'.", "The meeting schedule has an exceptDate of '2024-01-01T10:00:00'.", "The bus route schedule lists '2023-11-05' as an exceptDate."
exchangeRateSpread: An ExchangeRateSpecification has an exchangeRateSpread that represents the difference between the buying and selling prices of foreign currency by an intermediary. Also called "currency spread", "broker's margin", "bid-ask spread". Examples: "The exchangeRateSpecification shows an exchangeRateSpread of '0.02 USD'.", "This exchangeRateSpecification has an exchangeRateSpread of '0.5%'.", "The exchangeRateSpread for the currency pair is '0.005'."
executableLibraryName: An APIReference has an executableLibraryName that specifies the file name of the library containing the API. Also called "library filename", "API library name", "module name". Examples: "The APIReference lists 'kernel32.dll' as its executableLibraryName.", "This APIReference has an executableLibraryName of 'libcurl.so'.", "The executableLibraryName for the API is 'my_library.jar'."
exerciseCourse: An ExerciseAction has an exerciseCourse that indicates the specific place or course where the exercise action was performed. Also called "workout location", "training course", "exercise venue". Examples: "The ExerciseAction took place on the 'running track' as its exerciseCourse.", "Her ExerciseAction had 'local gym' as its exerciseCourse.", "The exerciseCourse for the marathon training was 'Central Park loop'." Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any action's location.
exercisePlan: An ExerciseAction uses an exercisePlan, which is the structured plan followed during the exercise. Also called "workout regimen", "training schedule", "fitness plan". Examples: "The ExerciseAction followed an exercisePlan for 'strength building'.", "His ExerciseAction used an exercisePlan designed for 'marathon preparation'.", "The exercisePlan for the session was 'HIIT workout'." Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any tool or plan used in an action.
exerciseRelatedDiet: An ExerciseAction is associated with an exerciseRelatedDiet, which is the dietary regimen followed in conjunction with the exercise. Also called "workout diet", "fitness diet", "training nutrition". Examples: "The ExerciseAction was supported by an exerciseRelatedDiet focused on 'high protein intake'.", "Her ExerciseAction included an exerciseRelatedDiet of 'low-carb meals'.", "The exerciseRelatedDiet for the athlete was 'paleo'." Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any tool or plan used in an action.
exerciseType: An ExerciseAction or ExercisePlan has an exerciseType that describes the specific kind of physical activity involved. Also called "activity type", "workout category", "fitness modality". Examples: "The ExerciseAction's exerciseType is 'aerobics'.", "This ExercisePlan specifies 'strength training' as its exerciseType.", "The exerciseType for the session was 'yoga'."
exifData: An ImageObject contains exifData, which is the exchangeable image file format metadata embedded within the image. Also called "image metadata", "EXIF information", "photo data". Examples: "The ImageObject includes exifData showing the 'camera model'.", "This ImageObject has exifData indicating the 'exposure time'.", "The exifData for the photo contains 'GPS coordinates'."
expectedArrivalFrom: A ParcelDelivery has an expectedArrivalFrom date or datetime, indicating the earliest point in time the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called "earliest arrival date", "minimum delivery date", "arrival window start". Examples: "The ParcelDelivery has an expectedArrivalFrom of '2023-10-26'.", "The package's expectedArrivalFrom is '2023-10-27T09:00:00'.", "The expectedArrivalFrom for the delivery is 'tomorrow morning'." Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which specifies the latest arrival time.
expectedArrivalUntil: A ParcelDelivery has an expectedArrivalUntil date or datetime, indicating the latest point in time the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called "latest arrival date", "maximum delivery date", "arrival window end". Examples: "The ParcelDelivery has an expectedArrivalUntil of '2023-10-28'.", "The package's expectedArrivalUntil is '2023-10-27T17:00:00'.", "The expectedArrivalUntil for the delivery is 'end of day'." Distinct from expectedArrivalFrom, which specifies the earliest arrival time.
expectedPrognosis: A MedicalCondition has an expectedPrognosis that describes its likely short-term or long-term outcome. Also called "anticipated outcome", "medical outlook", "disease prognosis". Examples: "The MedicalCondition has an expectedPrognosis of 'full recovery'.", "This MedicalCondition's expectedPrognosis is 'chronic but manageable'.", "The expectedPrognosis for the illness is 'guarded'."
expectsAcceptanceOf: An ActionAccessSpecification, ConsumeAction, or MediaSubscription expectsAcceptanceOf an Offer that must be accepted before the user can perform the associated action. Also called "requires offer acceptance", "prerequisite offer", "offer to accept". Examples: "The ConsumeAction expectsAcceptanceOf a 'purchase offer' for the movie.", "This MediaSubscription expectsAcceptanceOf a 'monthly subscription offer'.", "The ActionAccessSpecification expectsAcceptanceOf a 'terms of service offer'."
experienceInPlaceOfEducation: A JobPosting has experienceInPlaceOfEducation, a boolean indicating if relevant work experience can substitute for formal educational qualifications. Also called "experience substitutes education", "education equivalency", "experience accepted for education". Examples: "The JobPosting has experienceInPlaceOfEducation set to 'true'.", "This JobPosting indicates experienceInPlaceOfEducation is 'false'.", "The job posting allows experienceInPlaceOfEducation."
experienceRequirements: A JobPosting or Occupation has experienceRequirements that describe the skills and prior work experience necessary for the role. Also called "required experience", "job experience", "occupational experience". Examples: "The JobPosting lists '5 years of project management' as its experienceRequirements.", "This Occupation has experienceRequirements for 'proficiency in Python'.", "The experienceRequirements include 'prior leadership roles'." Distinct from educationRequirements, which specifies formal educational qualifications.
expertConsiderations: A Diet includes expertConsiderations, which are medical expert advice pertinent to the dietary plan. Also called "medical advice", "dietary expert notes", "professional recommendations". Examples: "The Diet plan has expertConsiderations regarding 'allergy risks'.", "This Diet includes expertConsiderations about 'nutrient deficiencies'.", "The expertConsiderations for the diet mention 'consulting a doctor'."
expires: A Certification or CreativeWork expires on a specific Date or DateTime, after which it is no longer valid, useful, or available. Also called "valid until", "expiration date", "no longer available after". Examples: "The Certification expires on '2024-06-30'.", "This NewsArticle expires on '2023-12-31'.", "The video content expires at '2024-01-01T00:00:00'." Distinct from datePublished, which indicates when content was made available.
expressedIn: A Gene is expressedIn an AnatomicalStructure, AnatomicalSystem, BioChemEntity, or DefinedTerm, indicating where its activity has been experimentally observed. Also called "gene activity location", "found in", "active in". Examples: "The gene is expressedIn the 'brain'.", "This gene is expressedIn the 'digestive system'.", "Gene X is expressedIn 'liver tissue'."
extendedAddress: A PostalAddress has an extendedAddress that provides additional details like an apartment number, suite, or care-of information. Also called "address line 2", "apartment number", "suite number", "c/o". Examples: "The PostalAddress includes an extendedAddress of 'Apt 4B'.", "This PostalAddress has an extendedAddress 'c/o John Doe'.", "The extendedAddress is 'Suite 101'." Distinct from streetAddress, which is the primary street number and name.
familyName: A Person has a familyName, which is their last name. Also called "last name", "surname". Examples: "The Person's familyName is 'Smith'.", "Her familyName is 'Garcia'.", "His familyName is 'Chen'." Distinct from givenName, which is the first name.
fatContent: NutritionInformation includes fatContent, specifying the total mass of fat in grams. Also called "total fat", "grams of fat", "lipid content". Examples: "The NutritionInformation shows a fatContent of '10g'.", "This product's fatContent is '5 grams'.", "The fatContent per serving is '15g'." Distinct from fiberContent, which specifies the mass of fiber.
faxNumber: A ContactPoint, Organization, Person, or Place has a faxNumber, which is its telefacsimile number. Also called "facsimile number", "fax line". Examples: "The Organization's faxNumber is '+1-555-123-4567'.", "The ContactPoint lists '555-987-6543' as its faxNumber.", "Her faxNumber is '555-111-2222'." Distinct from telephone, which is a voice call number.
featureList: A SoftwareApplication has a featureList, detailing the functionalities or modules it provides. Also called "application features", "software capabilities", "module list". Examples: "The SoftwareApplication's featureList includes 'spell check' and 'grammar correction'.", "This application has a featureList of 'real-time collaboration'.", "The featureList for the software is available at 'example.com/features'."
feesAndCommissionsSpecification: A FinancialProduct or FinancialService has a feesAndCommissionsSpecification, which describes the applicable fees, commissions, and other terms. Also called "fee structure", "commission details", "pricing terms". Examples: "The FinancialProduct includes a feesAndCommissionsSpecification detailing 'annual maintenance fees'.", "This FinancialService has a feesAndCommissionsSpecification at 'bank.com/fees'.", "The feesAndCommissionsSpecification outlines 'transaction charges'."
fiberContent: NutritionInformation includes fiberContent, specifying the total mass of dietary fiber in grams. Also called "total fiber", "grams of fiber", "dietary fiber". Examples: "The NutritionInformation shows a fiberContent of '3g'.", "This product's fiberContent is '2 grams'.", "The fiberContent per serving is '5g'." Distinct from fatContent, which specifies the mass of fat.
fileFormat: A CreativeWork has a fileFormat, which specifies the media type or MIME format of its content. Also called "media type", "MIME type", "content format". Examples: "The CreativeWork has a fileFormat of 'image/jpeg'.", "This document's fileFormat is 'application/pdf'.", "The fileFormat for the video is 'video/mp4'." Distinct from encoding, which can describe multiple representations of a work, each with its own file format.
fileSize: A SoftwareApplication has a fileSize, indicating the size of its application or package. Also called "application size", "package size", "download size". Examples: "The SoftwareApplication has a fileSize of '250MB'.", "This application's fileSize is '12KB'.", "The fileSize is '500MB'."
financialAidEligible: A Course or EducationalOccupationalProgram is financialAidEligible for a specific type or program of financial assistance that students can use for tuition or fees. Also called "eligible for financial aid", "financial assistance program", "aid program". Examples: "The Course is financialAidEligible for 'Pell Grants'.", "This EducationalOccupationalProgram is financialAidEligible for 'federal student loans'.", "The program is financialAidEligible for 'scholarships'."
firstAppearance: A Claim has a firstAppearance in a CreativeWork, indicating where it was first known to occur. Also called "first mentioned in", "initially appeared in", "original publication". Examples: "The Claim's firstAppearance was in 'The New York Times article'.", "This Claim has its firstAppearance in 'a scientific paper'.", "The firstAppearance of the claim was in 'a blog post'."
firstPerformance: A MusicComposition has a firstPerformance, which is the Event where the work was initially performed. Also called "premiere performance", "initial staging", "debut performance". Examples: "The MusicComposition had its firstPerformance at 'Carnegie Hall'.", "This opera's firstPerformance was a 'gala event'.", "The firstPerformance of the symphony was in '1824'." Distinct from performance, which refers to any performance of the work.
flightDistance: A Flight has a flightDistance, specifying the total distance covered by the flight. Also called "distance flown", "flight length", "route distance". Examples: "The Flight has a flightDistance of '1500 miles'.", "This Flight's flightDistance is '2400 km'.", "The flightDistance was 'short-haul'."
flightNumber: A Flight has a flightNumber, which is its unique identifier including the airline IATA code. Also called "flight ID", "airline flight code", "flight identifier". Examples: "The Flight's flightNumber is 'UA110'.", "This Flight has a flightNumber of 'BA249'.", "The flightNumber for the journey is 'DL88'."
floorLevel: An Accommodation, LocalBusiness, or Residence has a floorLevel, indicating its specific floor within a multi-storey building. Also called "level number", "storey", "floor number". Examples: "The Accommodation is on floorLevel '3'.", "This LocalBusiness has a floorLevel of 'Ground Floor'.", "The Residence's floorLevel is 'Penthouse'."
floorLimit: A PaymentCard has a floorLimit, which is the monetary amount above which credit card transactions require authorization. Also called "authorization threshold", "transaction limit", "credit card limit". Examples: "The PaymentCard has a floorLimit of '$500'.", "This card's floorLimit is '€1000'.", "The floorLimit for the transaction is '$200'." Distinct from creditLimit, which is the total amount of credit available.
floorSize: An Accommodation or FloorPlan has a floorSize, specifying its area, typically in square meters or square feet. Also called "area", "square footage", "room size". Examples: "The Accommodation has a floorSize of '120 square meters'.", "This FloorPlan shows a floorSize of '800 sq ft'.", "The floorSize of the apartment is '75 MTK'."
followee: A FollowAction has a followee, which is the Organization or Person being followed. Also called "person followed", "organization followed", "followed entity". Examples: "The FollowAction's followee is 'Jane Doe'.", "This FollowAction targets 'Acme Corp' as its followee.", "The followee of the action is 'a public figure'." Distinct from object, which is a more general property for the object of any action.
follows: A Person follows another Person, indicating a uni-directional social relation where the subject observes or tracks the object. Also called "is following", "subscribes to", "tracks". Examples: "John follows 'Mary'.", "She follows 'her favorite artist'.", "The user follows 'a news account'." Distinct from knows, which implies a mutual acquaintance.
followup: A MedicalProcedure has a followup, which describes the typical or recommended care after the procedure. Also called "post-procedure care", "aftercare instructions", "follow-up treatment". Examples: "The MedicalProcedure includes followup instructions for 'rest and medication'.", "This procedure's followup specifies 'a check-up in two weeks'.", "The followup care involves 'physical therapy'."
foodEstablishment: A CookAction takes place at a foodEstablishment, which is the specific food-related business or place where the cooking occurred. Also called "cooking location", "restaurant", "kitchen". Examples: "The CookAction happened at the 'local diner' as its foodEstablishment.", "This CookAction's foodEstablishment was 'a gourmet restaurant'.", "The foodEstablishment for the event was 'the community kitchen'." Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any action's location.
foodEvent: A CookAction takes place at a foodEvent, which is the specific event focused on food where the cooking occurred. Also called "culinary event", "cooking event location", "food festival". Examples: "The CookAction occurred at the 'annual food festival' as its foodEvent.", "This CookAction's foodEvent was 'a charity bake-off'.", "The foodEvent for the competition was 'the chili cook-off'." Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any action's location.
foodWarning: A Drug has a foodWarning, providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding the consumption of specific foods while taking the drug. Also called "dietary restrictions", "food interaction warning", "drug-food precautions". Examples: "The Drug includes a foodWarning about 'grapefruit juice'.", "This Drug has a foodWarning advising against 'dairy products'.", "The foodWarning states 'avoid alcohol'." Distinct from drugWarning, which is a general warning about the drug itself.
founder: An Organization has a founder, which is the Person or Organization that established it. Also called "creator", "establisher", "originator". Examples: "The Organization's founder is 'Steve Jobs'.", "This company's founder is 'a group of scientists'.", "The founder of the startup is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from founders, which is a plural property for multiple founders.
founders: An Organization has founders, which are the Persons who established it. Also called "co-founders", "founding members", "originators". Examples: "The Organization's founders are 'Larry Page and Sergey Brin'.", "This company's founders include 'three university students'.", "The founders of the non-profit are 'a group of activists'." Distinct from founder, which is a singular property for one founder.
foundingDate: An Organization has a foundingDate, which is the specific date when it was established. Also called "establishment date", "date founded", "inception date". Examples: "The Organization's foundingDate is '1976-04-01'.", "This company's foundingDate is '2005-02-14'.", "The foundingDate of the institution is '1888'."
foundingLocation: An Organization has a foundingLocation, which is the specific place where it was established. Also called "place of origin", "establishment location", "birthplace". Examples: "The Organization's foundingLocation is 'Menlo Park, California'.", "This company's foundingLocation is 'a garage in Silicon Valley'.", "The foundingLocation of the university is 'Cambridge, England'." Distinct from location, which is a general current location.
free: A PublicationEvent has a 'free' boolean flag, indicating whether the item, event, or place is accessible without cost. Also called "no cost", "gratis", "complimentary access". Examples: "The PublicationEvent is free, meaning 'true'.", "This event is free.", "The concert is free to attend." Distinct from price, which specifies a monetary cost.
freeShippingThreshold: ShippingRateSettings has a freeShippingThreshold, which is a monetary value at or above which shipping becomes free. Also called "free delivery minimum", "shipping cost waiver", "minimum for free shipping". Examples: "The ShippingRateSettings specifies a freeShippingThreshold of '$50'.", "This setting has a freeShippingThreshold of '€75'.", "The freeShippingThreshold is '$100'." Distinct from shippingRate, which is the actual cost of shipping.
frequency: A DoseSchedule has a frequency, describing how often a dose should be taken. Also called "dosage frequency", "how often", "rate of administration". Examples: "The DoseSchedule specifies a frequency of 'daily'.", "This medication has a frequency of 'twice a day'.", "The frequency for the dose is 'every four hours'." Distinct from doseValue, which specifies the amount of the dose.
fromLocation: An ExerciseAction, MoveAction, or TransferAction has a fromLocation, indicating the starting place of the object or agent before the action. Also called "origin location", "starting point", "departure location". Examples: "The MoveAction's fromLocation is 'New York'.", "This TransferAction originated from 'Warehouse A'.", "The ExerciseAction started from 'the gym'." Distinct from location, which is a general location, and toLocation, which is the destination.
fuelCapacity: A Vehicle has a fuelCapacity, which is the total storage capacity of its fuel tank or battery. Also called "tank capacity", "battery capacity", "fuel tank size". Examples: "The Vehicle has a fuelCapacity of '60 LTR'.", "This electric car's fuelCapacity is '75 kWh'.", "The fuelCapacity of the truck is '20 GLL'." Distinct from fuelConsumption, which is the rate of fuel use.
fuelConsumption: A Vehicle has a fuelConsumption, indicating the amount of fuel used over a specific distance or duration. Also called "fuel usage", "gas consumption", "liters per 100km". Examples: "The Vehicle has a fuelConsumption of '8 L/100 km'.", "This car's fuelConsumption is '12 liters per 100 km'.", "The fuelConsumption is 'high in city traffic'." Distinct from fuelEfficiency, which is the reciprocal measure (distance per unit fuel).
fuelEfficiency: A Vehicle has a fuelEfficiency, indicating the distance it can travel per unit of fuel used. Also called "miles per gallon", "km per liter", "fuel economy". Examples: "The Vehicle has a fuelEfficiency of '30 mpg'.", "This car's fuelEfficiency is '15 km/L'.", "The fuelEfficiency is 'excellent on highways'." Distinct from fuelConsumption, which is the reciprocal measure (fuel per unit distance).
fuelType: An EngineSpecification or Vehicle has a fuelType, specifying the kind of fuel suitable for its engine(s). Also called "engine fuel", "gas type", "power source". Examples: "The Vehicle's fuelType is 'gasoline'.", "This EngineSpecification requires 'diesel' as its fuelType.", "The fuelType for the car is 'electric'."
fulfillmentType: A ShippingService has a fulfillmentType, which specifies the method of fulfilling the order. Also called "delivery method", "order fulfillment method", "shipping method". Examples: "The ShippingService has a fulfillmentType of 'Delivery'.", "This ShippingService's fulfillmentType is 'Pickup'.", "The fulfillmentType is 'Ship'."
functionalClass: A Joint has a functionalClass, describing the degree of mobility it allows. Also called "joint mobility", "range of motion", "joint classification". Examples: "The Joint has a functionalClass of 'synarthrosis'.", "This joint's functionalClass is 'amphiarthrosis'.", "The functionalClass of the knee is 'diarthrosis'." Distinct from structuralClass, which describes the anatomical structure of the joint.
fundedItem: A Grant funds a fundedItem, which is a BioChemEntity, CreativeWork, Event, MedicalEntity, Organization, Person, or Product that receives direct or indirect financial support. Also called "grant recipient", "sponsored item", "supported project". Examples: "The Grant supports a fundedItem that is 'a research project'.", "This Grant's fundedItem is 'a new medical device'.", "The fundedItem is 'a non-profit organization'." Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the grant.
funder: A CreativeWork, Event, Grant, MonetaryGrant, Organization, or Person has a funder, which is the Organization or Person providing financial support or sponsorship. Also called "sponsor", "grantor", "financial supporter". Examples: "The CreativeWork's funder is 'the National Endowment for the Arts'.", "This Event has 'Acme Corp' as its funder.", "The funder of the research is 'a private foundation'." Distinct from fundedItem, which is the entity receiving the funding.
funding: A BioChemEntity, CreativeWork, Event, MedicalEntity, Organization, Person, or Product receives funding through a Grant that provides direct or indirect financial support. Also called "grant received", "sponsored by", "supported by grant". Examples: "The CreativeWork received funding from 'Grant X'.", "This research project has funding from 'a federal grant'.", "The organization's funding comes from 'multiple grants'." Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the funding.
game: A GameServer hosts a game, which is the VideoGame played on that server. Also called "hosted game", "server game", "game title". Examples: "The GameServer hosts the game 'Minecraft'.", "This GameServer runs the game 'Fortnite'.", "The game played on the server is 'League of Legends'."
gameAvailabilityType: A PlayGameAction has a gameAvailabilityType, indicating whether the game content is a full version, demo, or other availability type. Also called "game version type", "availability status", "content type". Examples: "The PlayGameAction has a gameAvailabilityType of 'Demo'.", "This action is for a gameAvailabilityType of 'FullGame'.", "The gameAvailabilityType is 'EarlyAccess'."
gameEdition: A VideoGame has a gameEdition, specifying a particular version or release of the game. Also called "game version", "edition name", "release edition". Examples: "The VideoGame is the 'Collector's Edition' as its gameEdition.", "This VideoGame has a gameEdition of 'Deluxe Edition'.", "The gameEdition is 'Standard'."
gameItem: A Game or VideoGameSeries includes a gameItem, which is an object within the game world that can be collected. Also called "in-game item", "collectible", "game object". Examples: "The Game features a gameItem called 'Health Potion'.", "This VideoGameSeries includes a gameItem like 'a rare sword'.", "The gameItem is 'a gold coin'."
gameLocation: A Game or VideoGameSeries has a gameLocation, which is a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called "game setting", "in-game location", "virtual world". Examples: "The Game's gameLocation is 'Hyrule'.", "This VideoGameSeries is set in a gameLocation of 'post-apocalyptic Earth'.", "The gameLocation is 'a medieval castle'." Distinct from location, which is a general location for any entity.
gamePlatform: A VideoGame or VideoGameSeries is played on a gamePlatform, which is the electronic system used to play it. Also called "gaming platform", "console", "system requirements". Examples: "The VideoGame is available on the gamePlatform 'PlayStation 5'.", "This VideoGameSeries supports the gamePlatform 'PC'.", "The gamePlatform is 'Xbox Series X'."
gameServer: A VideoGame can be played on a gameServer, which is the server hosting the game. Also called "hosting server", "game host", "multiplayer server". Examples: "The VideoGame connects to a gameServer for online play.", "This VideoGame uses a dedicated gameServer.", "The gameServer is located in 'Europe'." Distinct from game, which is the game itself.
gameTip: A VideoGame has a gameTip, which is a CreativeWork providing tips, tactics, or strategies for playing the game. Also called "game guide", "strategy guide", "game hints". Examples: "The VideoGame has a gameTip for 'defeating the final boss'.", "This VideoGame includes a gameTip on 'leveling up quickly'.", "The gameTip provides 'advanced combat strategies'."
gender: A Person or SportsTeam has a gender, indicating their gender identity or the gender composition of the team. Also called "sex", "gender identity", "team gender". Examples: "The Person's gender is 'Female'.", "This SportsTeam has a gender of 'Mixed'.", "The character's gender is 'Non-binary'."
genre: A BroadcastChannel, CreativeWork, or MusicGroup has a genre, which is its category or style. Also called "category", "style", "type". Examples: "The CreativeWork's genre is 'Science Fiction'.", "This MusicGroup plays 'Rock' genre music.", "The BroadcastChannel features 'News' as its genre." Distinct from keywords, which are descriptive terms rather than a classification.
geo: A Place has geo information, which specifies its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called "geolocation", "geographic coordinates", "map data". Examples: "The Place has geo coordinates of '34.0522, -118.2437'.", "This Place's geo is a 'GeoShape representing a park'.", "The geo for the city is 'a polygon boundary'." Distinct from address, which is a postal address.
geoContains: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoContains another GeospatialGeometry or Place if the subject completely encloses the object, with at least one interior point of the object also in the interior of the subject. Also called "encloses", "encompasses", "has within". Examples: "The country geoContains 'a specific city'.", "The park geoContains 'a playground'.", "The polygon geoContains 'a smaller polygon'." Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relationship (object is within subject).
geoCoveredBy: A GeospatialGeometry or Place is geoCoveredBy another GeospatialGeometry or Place if the subject is entirely covered by the object. Also called "is covered by", "lies within", "is encompassed by". Examples: "The city is geoCoveredBy 'the state'.", "The small island is geoCoveredBy 'the ocean'.", "The point is geoCoveredBy 'the polygon'." Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relationship (subject covers object).
geoCovers: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoCovers another GeospatialGeometry or Place if every point of the object is also a point of the subject's interior or boundary. Also called "covers", "encompasses", "extends over". Examples: "The state geoCovers 'the city'.", "The ocean geoCovers 'the small island'.", "The polygon geoCovers 'the point'." Distinct from geoCoveredBy, which is the inverse relationship (object is covered by subject).
geoCrosses: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoCrosses another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they intersect such that their common interior points form a geometry of a lower dimension than at least one of them. Also called "intersects and passes through", "crosses over", "traverses". Examples: "A road geoCrosses 'a river'.", "The flight path geoCrosses 'several states'.", "A line segment geoCrosses 'a polygon'." Distinct from geoIntersects, which is a more general intersection.
geoDisjoint: A GeospatialGeometry or Place is geoDisjoint from another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they have no points in common and are topologically disconnected. Also called "separate from", "not overlapping", "disconnected from". Examples: "Two islands are geoDisjoint.", "The two buildings are geoDisjoint.", "The point is geoDisjoint from 'the polygon'." Distinct from geoIntersects, which implies common points.
geoEquals: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoEquals another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they are topologically identical, meaning their interiors intersect and neither's interior or boundary intersects the other's exterior. Also called "is geographically equal to", "same location as", "identical geometry". Examples: "Two representations of the same park geoEquals each other.", "The administrative boundary geoEquals 'the natural boundary'.", "The two polygons geoEquals if they define the exact same area."
geoIntersects: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoIntersects another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they share at least one common point. Also called "overlaps with", "touches", "crosses". Examples: "The road geoIntersects 'the forest'.", "The two cities' boundaries geoIntersects.", "The point geoIntersects 'the line'." Distinct from geoDisjoint, which means no common points.
geoMidpoint: A GeoCircle has a geoMidpoint, which specifies the GeoCoordinates at its center. Also called "center coordinates", "geographic center", "central point". Examples: "The GeoCircle has a geoMidpoint of '34.05, -118.25'.", "This GeoCircle's geoMidpoint is 'the city center'.", "The geoMidpoint for the circular region is 'the exact middle'."
geoOverlaps: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoOverlaps another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they share some but not all points in common. Also called "partially overlaps", "shares area with", "intersects partially". Examples: "The two districts geoOverlaps.", "The park geoOverlaps 'the residential area'.", "The two polygons geoOverlaps slightly." Distinct from geoIntersects, which is more general and includes touching or containing.
geoRadius: A GeoCircle has a geoRadius, which specifies its approximate radius, typically in meters. Also called "circle radius", "geographic radius", "distance from center". Examples: "The GeoCircle has a geoRadius of '1000 meters'.", "This GeoCircle's geoRadius is '5 km'.", "The geoRadius is '2 miles'." Distinct from geoMidpoint, which is the center point.
geoTouches: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoTouches another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they share at least one boundary point but no interior points. Also called "borders", "adjoins", "is adjacent to". Examples: "Two adjacent properties geoTouches.", "The river geoTouches 'the forest edge'.", "The two polygons geoTouches at a shared boundary." Distinct from geoIntersects, which includes overlapping interiors.
geoWithin: A GeospatialGeometry or Place is geoWithin another GeospatialGeometry or Place if the subject is entirely contained within the interior of the object. Also called "is inside", "located within", "contained by". Examples: "The city is geoWithin 'the state'.", "The building is geoWithin 'the property boundary'.", "The point is geoWithin 'the polygon'." Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relationship (subject contains object).
geographicArea: An Audience is associated with a geographicArea, which is the administrative area relevant to that audience. Also called "target region", "audience location", "service area". Examples: "The Audience's geographicArea is 'California'.", "This Audience targets the geographicArea 'Europe'.", "The geographicArea for the campaign is 'New York City'."
gettingTestedInfo: A SpecialAnnouncement provides gettingTestedInfo, which is a URL or WebContent offering information about testing for a medical condition. Also called "testing information", "how to get tested", "testing guidance". Examples: "The SpecialAnnouncement includes gettingTestedInfo at 'health.gov/testing'.", "This announcement provides gettingTestedInfo about 'COVID-19 testing sites'.", "The gettingTestedInfo is a 'web page with local testing options'." Distinct from diseasePreventionInfo, which is about preventing the disease.
givenName: A Person has a givenName, which is their first name. Also called "first name", "personal name". Examples: "The Person's givenName is 'John'.", "Her givenName is 'Maria'.", "His givenName is 'David'." Distinct from familyName, which is the last name.
globalLocationNumber: An Organization, Person, or Place has a globalLocationNumber (GLN), which is a 13-digit identifier for parties and physical locations. Also called "GLN", "International Location Number", "ILN". Examples: "The Organization's globalLocationNumber is '1234567890123'.", "This Place has a globalLocationNumber of '9876543210987'.", "The globalLocationNumber identifies the warehouse." Distinct from identifier, which is a general identifier.
governmentBenefitsInfo: A SpecialAnnouncement provides governmentBenefitsInfo, which is a GovernmentService offering details about associated government benefits. Also called "government aid information", "public assistance details", "benefit program info". Examples: "The SpecialAnnouncement includes governmentBenefitsInfo about 'unemployment benefits'.", "This announcement provides governmentBenefitsInfo on 'housing assistance programs'.", "The governmentBenefitsInfo describes 'small business grants'."
gracePeriod: A LoanOrCredit has a gracePeriod, which is the duration after a due date during which a borrower can fulfill obligations before defaulting. Also called "payment grace period", "default deferral period", "late payment window". Examples: "The LoanOrCredit has a gracePeriod of '15 days'.", "This loan's gracePeriod is 'one month'.", "The gracePeriod for the credit card is '21 days'." Distinct from loanRepaymentForm, which describes the repayment structure.
grantee: A DigitalDocumentPermission is granted to a grantee, which is the Audience, ContactPoint, Organization, or Person receiving the permission. Also called "permission recipient", "authorized party", "beneficiary". Examples: "The DigitalDocumentPermission is granted to the grantee 'John Doe'.", "This permission's grantee is 'the marketing department'.", "The grantee is 'any registered user'." Distinct from grantor, which is the entity giving the permission.
greater: A QualitativeValue is greater than another QualitativeValue, indicating that the subject holds a higher position in an ordered sequence than the object. Also called "is greater than", "exceeds", "is superior to". Examples: "A 'High' rating is greater than 'Medium'.", "The value 'Excellent' is greater than 'Good'.", "The QualitativeValue 'Large' is greater than 'Small'." Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.
greaterOrEqual: A QualitativeValue is greaterOrEqual to another QualitativeValue, indicating that the subject holds a higher or equal position in an ordered sequence than the object. Also called "is greater than or equal to", "at least", "not less than". Examples: "A 'High' rating is greaterOrEqual to 'Medium'.", "The value 'Good' is greaterOrEqual to 'Good'.", "The QualitativeValue 'Large' is greaterOrEqual to 'Medium'." Distinct from greater, which strictly excludes equality.
gtin: A Demand, Offer, or Product has a gtin, which is its Global Trade Item Number, a numeric identifier for trade items. Also called "Global Trade Item Number", "product identifier", "barcode number". Examples: "The Product has a gtin of '0123456789012'.", "This Offer's gtin is 'https://example.com/gtin/1234567890123'.", "The gtin identifies the specific product variant." Distinct from sku, which is a stock-keeping unit for internal use.
gtin12: A Demand, Offer, or Product has a gtin12, which is its 12-digit Global Trade Item Number (UPC). Also called "UPC code", "GTIN-12", "product barcode". Examples: "The Product has a gtin12 of '012345678901'.", "This Offer's gtin12 is '789012345678'.", "The gtin12 identifies the item in North America." Distinct from gtin, which is a general GTIN, and gtin13, gtin14, gtin8 for other specific GTIN lengths.
gtin13: A Demand, Offer, or Product has a gtin13, which is its 13-digit Global Trade Item Number (EAN/UCC-13 or ISBN). Also called "EAN-13", "ISBN-13", "GTIN-13". Examples: "The Product has a gtin13 of '1234567890128'.", "This Offer's gtin13 is '9780321765723'.", "The gtin13 identifies the item in Europe." Distinct from gtin, which is a general GTIN, and gtin12, gtin14, gtin8 for other specific GTIN lengths.
gtin14: A Demand, Offer, or Product has a gtin14, which is its 14-digit Global Trade Item Number, often used for trade items at different packaging levels. Also called "GTIN-14", "shipping container code", "case code". Examples: "The Product has a gtin14 of '10012345678905'.", "This Offer's gtin14 is '00012345678901'.", "The gtin14 identifies a carton of products." Distinct from gtin, which is a general GTIN, and gtin12, gtin13, gtin8 for other specific GTIN lengths.
gtin8: A Demand, Offer, or Product has a gtin8, which is its 8-digit Global Trade Item Number (EAN/UCC-8). Also called "EAN-8", "GTIN-8", "short EAN". Examples: "The Product has a gtin8 of '12345670'.", "This Offer's gtin8 is '98765432'.", "The gtin8 identifies small consumer goods." Distinct from gtin, which is a general GTIN, and gtin12, gtin13, gtin14 for other specific GTIN lengths.
guideline: A MedicalEntity is associated with a guideline, which is a MedicalGuideline providing recommendations or instructions related to it. Also called "medical recommendation", "clinical guideline", "best practice". Examples: "The MedicalEntity has a guideline for 'treatment protocols'.", "This condition is covered by a guideline on 'diagnosis procedures'.", "The guideline provides advice on 'patient care'." Distinct from code, which is a medical code.
guidelineDate: A MedicalGuideline has a guidelineDate, which is the date when its recommendations were issued. Also called "recommendation date", "issuance date", "publication date". Examples: "The MedicalGuideline has a guidelineDate of '2022-01-15'.", "This guideline's guidelineDate is '2023-03-01'.", "The guidelineDate indicates when the advice was last updated." Distinct from datePublished, which is a general publication date for any creative work.
guidelineSubject: A MedicalGuideline has a guidelineSubject, which is the MedicalEntity (e.g., condition or treatment) that the guideline addresses. Also called "guideline topic", "subject of guideline", "medical focus". Examples: "The MedicalGuideline's guidelineSubject is 'Type 2 Diabetes'.", "This guideline has a guidelineSubject of 'Chemotherapy'.", "The guidelineSubject is 'pediatric care'."
handlingTime: handlingTime describes the typical duration a ShippingDeliveryTime or ShippingService takes to process an order before the goods are dispatched or ready for pickup. Also called "processing time", "preparation time", "dispatch time", "order fulfillment time". Examples: A ShippingDeliveryTime has a handlingTime of "2 business days". A ShippingService has a handlingTime of "1-3 days". A ShippingDeliveryTime has a handlingTime of a ServicePeriod specifying a cut-off time and duration.
hasAdultConsideration: hasAdultConsideration indicates that an Offer or Product is intended or suitable for consumption or use by adults only. Also called "adult-oriented", "for adults only", "age-restricted", "adult content". Examples: A Product hasAdultConsideration set to "AdultSexualContent". An Offer hasAdultConsideration indicating "explicit content". A VideoGame hasAdultConsideration for "mature themes".
hasBioChemEntityPart: hasBioChemEntityPart indicates that a BioChemEntity (the whole) contains another BioChemEntity (the part) as a component. Also called "composed of", "contains component", "includes part". Examples: A Protein hasBioChemEntityPart an AminoAcid. A Gene hasBioChemEntityPart a Nucleotide. A Cell hasBioChemEntityPart a Mitochondrion.
hasBioPolymerSequence: hasBioPolymerSequence provides a symbolic representation of a Gene's nucleotide sequence or a Protein's amino acid sequence. Also called "sequence representation", "genetic sequence", "amino acid sequence". Examples: A Gene hasBioPolymerSequence "ATGC...". A Protein hasBioPolymerSequence "AGCT...". A BioChemEntity hasBioPolymerSequence a Text string representing its structure.
hasBroadcastChannel: hasBroadcastChannel identifies a specific BroadcastChannel that is part of a BroadcastService. Also called "channel offered by", "service channel". Examples: A BroadcastService hasBroadcastChannel "BBC One". A TV service hasBroadcastChannel "Channel 4". A radio service hasBroadcastChannel "Radio X".
hasCategoryCode: hasCategoryCode specifies a CategoryCode that is included within a CategoryCodeSet. Also called "includes code", "contains category". Examples: A CategoryCodeSet hasCategoryCode "ProductCategory". A CodeSet hasCategoryCode "MedicalSpecialty". A ClassificationSystem hasCategoryCode "NAICS Code".
hasCertification: hasCertification provides information about a Certification awarded to an Organization, Person, Place, Product, or Service. Also called "holds certification", "is certified by", "certification details". Examples: An Organization hasCertification "ISO 9001". A Person hasCertification "PMP". A Product hasCertification "Energy Star". A Service hasCertification "Organic Certified".
hasCourse: hasCourse identifies a Course that is one of the learning opportunities constituting an EducationalOccupationalProgram. Also called "program includes course", "contains course", "course component". Examples: An EducationalOccupationalProgram hasCourse "Introduction to Programming". A DegreeProgram hasCourse "Calculus I". A VocationalTraining hasCourse "Welding Basics".
hasCourseInstance: hasCourseInstance specifies a particular offering of a Course at a specific time, place, or through specific media. Also called "course offering", "instance of course", "scheduled course". Examples: A Course hasCourseInstance "Fall 2023, Online". A UniversityCourse hasCourseInstance "Section A, Tuesdays 10 AM". A CookingClass hasCourseInstance "July 15th, Downtown Studio".
hasCredential: hasCredential indicates a Credential that has been awarded to a Person or Organization. Also called "holds credential", "awarded credential", "credential details". Examples: A Person hasCredential "PhD in Computer Science". An Organization hasCredential "Accredited Business". A Doctor hasCredential "Medical License".
hasDefinedTerm: hasDefinedTerm specifies a DefinedTerm that is included within a DefinedTermSet or Taxon. Also called "includes term", "contains definition". Examples: A DefinedTermSet hasDefinedTerm "MedicalCondition". A Taxon hasDefinedTerm "Homo sapiens". A Glossary hasDefinedTerm "Algorithm".
hasDeliveryMethod: hasDeliveryMethod indicates the DeliveryMethod used for a DeliveryEvent or ParcelDelivery. Also called "delivery via", "shipping method", "transport method". Examples: A ParcelDelivery hasDeliveryMethod "ShippingDelivery". A DeliveryEvent hasDeliveryMethod "OnSitePickup". An Order hasDeliveryMethod "ExpressShipping".
hasDigitalDocumentPermission: hasDigitalDocumentPermission specifies a DigitalDocumentPermission related to the access (e.g., read or write) of a DigitalDocument. Also called "document access rights", "permission for document", "document permissions". Examples: A DigitalDocument hasDigitalDocumentPermission for "read access" by "public". A Report hasDigitalDocumentPermission for "edit access" by "team members". A Contract hasDigitalDocumentPermission for "view only" by "client".
hasDriveThroughService: hasDriveThroughService indicates whether a Place offers a service that can be used by driving through in a car. Also called "offers drive-through", "drive-in service available". Examples: A FoodEstablishment hasDriveThroughService true. A CovidTestingFacility hasDriveThroughService true. A Bank hasDriveThroughService true.
hasEnergyConsumptionDetails: hasEnergyConsumptionDetails defines the EnergyConsumptionDetails for a Product, specifying its energy efficiency category according to a standard. Also called "energy rating details", "efficiency information". Examples: A Refrigerator hasEnergyConsumptionDetails for "Energy Star A++". A WashingMachine hasEnergyConsumptionDetails specifying its energy class. A Product hasEnergyConsumptionDetails describing its consumption metrics.
hasEnergyEfficiencyCategory: hasEnergyEfficiencyCategory defines the EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration (category or rating) for a product within its EnergyConsumptionDetails. Also called "energy class", "efficiency rating". Examples: EnergyConsumptionDetails hasEnergyEfficiencyCategory "A++". A Product's energy details hasEnergyEfficiencyCategory "EnergyStarCertified". EnergyConsumptionDetails hasEnergyEfficiencyCategory "Class B".
hasGS1DigitalLink: hasGS1DigitalLink provides the GS1 digital link (URL) associated with an Offer, Organization, Place, or Product, conforming to digital link requirements. Also called "GS1 link", "product digital link", "item identifier URL". Examples: A Product hasGS1DigitalLink "https://id.gs1.org/01/12345678901232". An Organization hasGS1DigitalLink for its global location number. An Offer hasGS1DigitalLink pointing to product information.
hasHealthAspect: hasHealthAspect indicates the specific HealthAspectEnumeration addressed in some HealthTopicContent, such as an overview or treatment information. Also called "health topic aspect", "content focus". Examples: HealthTopicContent hasHealthAspect "Treatment". A MedicalArticle hasHealthAspect "Overview". A HealthGuide hasHealthAspect "SelfCare".
hasMap: hasMap provides a URL to a map of the Place. Also called "map link", "location map", "geographic map". Examples: A Place hasMap "https://maps.google.com/place/...". A Restaurant hasMap a URL to its location. A Park hasMap an image of its layout.
hasMeasurement: hasMeasurement specifies a QuantitativeValue representing a measurement of an item, such as its size, weight, or carbon footprint. Also called "item measurement", "product dimension", "measured value". Examples: A Product hasMeasurement for its "inseam" of "32 inches". A Certification hasMeasurement for "carbon footprint" of "10 kg CO2e". An Offer hasMeasurement for "wheel size" of "26 inches".
hasMemberProgram: hasMemberProgram identifies a MemberProgram offered by an Organization. Also called "loyalty program", "membership scheme", "rewards program". Examples: An Organization hasMemberProgram "Frequent Flyer Program". A Retailer hasMemberProgram "Customer Loyalty Club". An Airline hasMemberProgram "Elite Status Program".
hasMenu: hasMenu provides the Menu for a FoodEstablishment, either as a structured representation, text, or a URL. Also called "restaurant menu", "food menu", "dining options". Examples: A FoodEstablishment hasMenu a URL to its online menu. A Restaurant hasMenu a structured Menu object. A Cafe hasMenu a Text description of daily specials.
hasMenuItem: hasMenuItem specifies a MenuItem that is contained within a Menu or MenuSection. Also called "menu item includes", "dish on menu", "food item". Examples: A Menu hasMenuItem "Spaghetti Carbonara". A MenuSection hasMenuItem "Caesar Salad". A DinnerMenu hasMenuItem "Grilled Salmon".
hasMenuSection: hasMenuSection specifies a MenuSection that is a subgrouping within a Menu or another MenuSection. Also called "menu subgroup", "menu category", "section of menu". Examples: A Menu hasMenuSection "Appetizers". A MenuSection hasMenuSection "Main Courses". A RestaurantMenu hasMenuSection "Desserts".
hasMerchantReturnPolicy: hasMerchantReturnPolicy specifies a MerchantReturnPolicy that may be applicable to an Offer, Organization, or Product. Also called "return policy details", "returns information", "customer return policy". Examples: An Offer hasMerchantReturnPolicy for "30-day returns". An Organization hasMerchantReturnPolicy for all its products. A Product hasMerchantReturnPolicy specifying conditions for returns.
hasMolecularFunction: hasMolecularFunction describes the Molecular function performed by a BioChemEntity, optionally including evidence via PropertyValue. Also called "molecular activity", "function of molecule". Examples: A Protein hasMolecularFunction "catalytic activity". A BioChemEntity hasMolecularFunction a DefinedTerm like "DNA binding". A Gene hasMolecularFunction a PropertyValue indicating its enzymatic role.
hasOccupation: hasOccupation describes the Occupation of a Person. Also called "person's job", "profession", "employment". Examples: A Person hasOccupation "Software Engineer". A Doctor hasOccupation "Cardiologist". A Student hasOccupation "Part-time Tutor".
hasOfferCatalog: hasOfferCatalog indicates an OfferCatalog listing for an Organization, Person, or Service. Also called "catalog of offers", "product catalog", "service listing". Examples: An Organization hasOfferCatalog for its entire product range. A Service hasOfferCatalog detailing available packages. A Retailer hasOfferCatalog of current promotions.
hasPOS: hasPOS identifies a Place that serves as a Point-of-Sale operated by an Organization or Person. Also called "point of sale location", "retail outlet", "store location". Examples: An Organization hasPOS "Main Street Store". A Retailer hasPOS "Online Shop". A Person hasPOS "Pop-up Market Stall".
hasPart: hasPart indicates an item or CreativeWork that is a component or segment of this item or CreativeWork. Also called "includes part", "contains component", "is composed of". Examples: A Book hasPart a "Chapter 1". A Car hasPart an "Engine". A CreativeWork hasPart another CreativeWork. Distinct from `isPartOf`, which indicates the reverse relationship (a part is part of a whole).
hasParticipationOffer: hasParticipationOffer specifies an Offer to participate in an Event, such as a Call for Proposals or Speakers. Also called "call for participation", "event offer". Examples: An Event hasParticipationOffer for "Call for Speakers". A Conference hasParticipationOffer for "Call for Papers". A Festival hasParticipationOffer for "Performer Applications".
hasRepresentation: hasRepresentation provides a common representation (e.g., protein sequence, chemical structure) for a BioChemEntity. Also called "molecular representation", "chemical structure", "sequence data". Examples: A BioChemEntity hasRepresentation "C6H12O6". A Protein hasRepresentation a Text string of its sequence. A Molecule hasRepresentation a PropertyValue describing its structure.
hasShippingService: hasShippingService specifies a ShippingService offered by an OfferShippingDetails or Organization. Also called "shipping options", "delivery service". Examples: An Organization hasShippingService "Standard Ground Shipping". OfferShippingDetails hasShippingService "Express Delivery". A Retailer hasShippingService "International Shipping".
hasSponsorshipOffer: hasSponsorshipOffer specifies an Offer to sponsor an Event, such as a Sponsorship Prospectus or Sponsor Packages. Also called "sponsorship opportunities", "sponsor offer". Examples: An Event hasSponsorshipOffer for "Platinum Sponsorship". A Conference hasSponsorshipOffer for "Exhibitor Packages". A CharityGala hasSponsorshipOffer for "Table Sponsorship".
hasStore: hasStore identifies an OnlineStore that is part of an OnlineMarketplace. Also called "marketplace store", "eCommerce store". Examples: An OnlineMarketplace hasStore "Amazon Books". An OnlineMarketplace hasStore "Etsy Shop". A DigitalPlatform hasStore "App Store".
hasTierBenefit: hasTierBenefit describes a TierBenefitEnumeration that is a benefit for a particular MemberProgramTier. Also called "tier perk", "membership benefit". Examples: A MemberProgramTier hasTierBenefit "Free Shipping". A GoldTier hasTierBenefit "Priority Support". A PremiumTier hasTierBenefit "Exclusive Access".
hasTierRequirement: hasTierRequirement specifies a requirement for a user to join a MemberProgramTier, such as a CreditCard, MonetaryAmount, or UnitPriceSpecification. Also called "tier eligibility", "membership criteria", "enrollment requirement". Examples: A MemberProgramTier hasTierRequirement a CreditCard for sign-up. A PremiumTier hasTierRequirement a MonetaryAmount of "$100 annual fee". A LoyaltyTier hasTierRequirement a UnitPriceSpecification for a periodic fee.
hasTiers: hasTiers specifies the MemberProgramTier levels that constitute a MemberProgram. Also called "program tiers", "membership levels". Examples: A MemberProgram hasTiers "Bronze, Silver, Gold". A LoyaltyProgram hasTiers "Basic, Premium, VIP". A SubscriptionService hasTiers "Free, Standard, Pro".
hasVariant: hasVariant indicates a Product that is a member or variation of a ProductGroup or ProductModel. Also called "product variation", "group member", "model variant". Examples: A ProductGroup hasVariant "Red T-shirt, size M". A ProductModel hasVariant "iPhone 15 Pro Max". A CarModel hasVariant "Sedan version".
headline: headline provides the main title or heading of a CreativeWork. Also called "title", "heading", "caption". Examples: A CreativeWork has a headline "Breaking News: Major Event Unfolds". An Article has a headline "New Study Reveals Health Benefits". A BlogPost has a headline "My Summer Vacation".
healthCondition: healthCondition specifies the MedicalCondition(s) of a Patient, MedicalStudy, or PeopleAudience. Also called "medical diagnosis", "patient condition", "target condition". Examples: A Patient has a healthCondition "Diabetes". A MedicalStudy targets a healthCondition "Hypertension". A PeopleAudience has a healthCondition "Asthma sufferers".
healthPlanCoinsuranceOption: healthPlanCoinsuranceOption describes whether the coinsurance applies before or after deductible for a HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification. Also called "coinsurance rule", "coinsurance application". Examples: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification has healthPlanCoinsuranceOption "After deductible". A HealthPlan has healthPlanCoinsuranceOption "Before deductible".
healthPlanCoinsuranceRate: healthPlanCoinsuranceRate specifies the rate of coinsurance as a number between 0.0 and 1.0 for a HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification. Also called "coinsurance percentage", "coinsurance ratio". Examples: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification has healthPlanCoinsuranceRate "0.2" (20%). A HealthPlan has healthPlanCoinsuranceRate "0.1".
healthPlanCopay: healthPlanCopay specifies the copay amount as a PriceSpecification for a HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification. Also called "copayment amount", "fixed fee". Examples: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification has healthPlanCopay a PriceSpecification of "$20". A HealthPlan has healthPlanCopay "$15 per visit".
healthPlanCopayOption: healthPlanCopayOption describes whether the copay applies before or after deductible for a HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification. Also called "copay rule", "copay application". Examples: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification has healthPlanCopayOption "Before deductible". A HealthPlan has healthPlanCopayOption "After deductible".
healthPlanCostSharing: healthPlanCostSharing indicates the costs to the patient for services under a HealthPlanFormulary or HealthPlanNetwork, either as a Boolean or a HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification. Also called "patient costs", "cost sharing details". Examples: A HealthPlanFormulary has healthPlanCostSharing true (cost sharing applies). A HealthPlanNetwork has healthPlanCostSharing a HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification. A Formulary has healthPlanCostSharing indicating specific patient costs.
healthPlanDrugOption: healthPlanDrugOption provides additional details or options related to drugs offered by a HealthInsurancePlan. Also called "drug coverage option", "pharmacy benefit option". Examples: A HealthInsurancePlan has healthPlanDrugOption "Mail-order pharmacy". A HealthPlan has healthPlanDrugOption "Generic drug preference".
healthPlanDrugTier: healthPlanDrugTier specifies the tier(s) of drugs offered by a HealthInsurancePlan or HealthPlanFormulary. Also called "drug formulary tier", "medication tier". Examples: A HealthInsurancePlan has healthPlanDrugTier "Tier 1 (Preferred Generics)". A HealthPlanFormulary has healthPlanDrugTier "Tier 3 (Non-Preferred Brand)".
healthPlanId: healthPlanId provides the unique 14-character, HIOS-generated Plan ID number for a HealthInsurancePlan. Also called "insurance plan ID", "HIOS plan number". Examples: A HealthInsurancePlan has healthPlanId "12345CA0010001". A MedicalPlan has healthPlanId "HIOS-XYZ-789".
healthPlanMarketingUrl: healthPlanMarketingUrl provides the URL that links directly to the plan brochure for a specific standard HealthInsurancePlan or plan variation. Also called "plan brochure URL", "insurance plan link". Examples: A HealthInsurancePlan has healthPlanMarketingUrl "https://example.com/plan-brochure.pdf". A MedicalPlan has healthPlanMarketingUrl to its official marketing page.
healthPlanNetworkId: healthPlanNetworkId provides the name or unique ID of a HealthPlanNetwork or MedicalOrganization. Also called "network ID", "provider network identifier". Examples: A HealthPlanNetwork has healthPlanNetworkId "PPO-Gold". A MedicalOrganization has healthPlanNetworkId "HMO-Plus".
healthPlanNetworkTier: healthPlanNetworkTier specifies the tier(s) for a HealthPlanNetwork. Also called "network level", "provider tier". Examples: A HealthPlanNetwork has healthPlanNetworkTier "Tier 1 (In-Network)". A ProviderNetwork has healthPlanNetworkTier "Tier 2 (Out-of-Network)".
healthPlanPharmacyCategory: healthPlanPharmacyCategory specifies the category or type of pharmacy associated with a HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification. Also called "pharmacy type", "drugstore category". Examples: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification has healthPlanPharmacyCategory "Retail Pharmacy". A HealthPlan has healthPlanPharmacyCategory "Specialty Pharmacy".
healthcareReportingData: healthcareReportingData indicates data describing a Hospital, such as a CDC CDCPMDRecord or a Dataset. Also called "hospital data", "reporting metrics". Examples: A Hospital has healthcareReportingData a CDCPMDRecord. A MedicalCenter has healthcareReportingData a Dataset of patient outcomes. A Clinic has healthcareReportingData for its bed occupancy.
height: height specifies the Distance or QuantitativeValue representing the height of a MediaObject, OfferShippingDetails, Person, Product, ShippingConditions, or VisualArtwork. Also called "item height", "vertical dimension", "stature". Examples: A Product has a height of "10 cm". A Person has a height of "1.8 meters". A VisualArtwork has a height of "24 inches".
highPrice: highPrice specifies the highest price of all offers available within an AggregateOffer. Also called "maximum price", "upper price limit". Examples: An AggregateOffer has a highPrice of "99.99". A ProductListing has a highPrice of "$500".
hiringOrganization: hiringOrganization identifies the Organization or Person offering the JobPosting. Also called "employer", "recruiting company", "job provider". Examples: A JobPosting has a hiringOrganization "Google". A JobPosting has a hiringOrganization "Acme Corp". A JobPosting has a hiringOrganization "Dr. Smith".
holdingArchive: holdingArchive identifies the ArchiveOrganization that holds, keeps, or maintains an ArchiveComponent. Also called "archive repository", "custodian archive". Examples: An ArchiveComponent has a holdingArchive "National Archives". A HistoricalDocument has a holdingArchive "University Library Special Collections".
homeLocation: homeLocation specifies a ContactPoint or Place representing a person's residence. Also called "residence address", "home address", "dwelling place". Examples: A Person has a homeLocation "123 Main St, Anytown". A Person has a homeLocation a ContactPoint for their home phone. A Person has a homeLocation a Place object for their apartment.
homeTeam: homeTeam identifies the Person or SportsTeam designated as the home team in a SportsEvent. Also called "host team", "local team". Examples: A SportsEvent has a homeTeam "New York Yankees". A FootballMatch has a homeTeam "FC Barcelona". A TennisMatch has a homeTeam "Serena Williams".
honorificPrefix: honorificPrefix provides an honorific prefix preceding a Person's name, such as Dr, Mrs, or Mr. Also called "title prefix", "courtesy title". Examples: A Person has an honorificPrefix "Dr.". A Person has an honorificPrefix "Ms.". A Person has an honorificPrefix "Prof.".
honorificSuffix: honorificSuffix provides an honorific suffix following a Person's name, such as M.D., PhD, or MSCSW. Also called "title suffix", "post-nominal letters". Examples: A Person has an honorificSuffix "M.D.". A Person has an honorificSuffix "PhD". A Person has an honorificSuffix "Esq.".
hospitalAffiliation: hospitalAffiliation indicates a Hospital with which a Physician or office is affiliated. Also called "affiliated hospital", "hospital connection". Examples: A Physician has a hospitalAffiliation "General Hospital". A Doctor'sOffice has a hospitalAffiliation "City Medical Center".
hostingOrganization: hostingOrganization identifies the Organization (e.g., airline, retailer) with which a MemberProgram or ProgramMembership is made or which offers it. Also called "program provider", "membership host". Examples: A MemberProgram has a hostingOrganization "United Airlines". A ProgramMembership has a hostingOrganization "Starbucks".
hoursAvailable: hoursAvailable specifies the OpeningHoursSpecification during which a ContactPoint, LocationFeatureSpecification, or Service is available. Also called "operating hours", "availability times", "service hours". Examples: A Service has hoursAvailable "Mon-Fri 9 AM - 5 PM". A ContactPoint has hoursAvailable for customer support. A LocationFeatureSpecification has hoursAvailable for access.
howPerformed: howPerformed describes the method or manner in which a MedicalProcedure is performed. Also called "procedure method", "execution details", "technique used". Examples: A MedicalProcedure has howPerformed "Laparoscopically". A Surgery has howPerformed "Open incision". A DiagnosticTest has howPerformed "Blood sample analysis".
httpMethod: httpMethod specifies the appropriate HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) for a request to an HTTP EntryPoint. Also called "HTTP verb", "request method". Examples: An EntryPoint has an httpMethod "GET". An APIEndpoint has an httpMethod "POST". A WebService has an httpMethod "PUT".
iataCode: iataCode provides the IATA identifier for an Airline or Airport. Also called "airline code", "airport code". Examples: An Airline has an iataCode "UA". An Airport has an iataCode "JFK". A Flight has an iataCode for its carrier.
icaoCode: icaoCode provides the ICAO identifier for an Airport. Also called "airport ICAO code". Examples: An Airport has an icaoCode "KJFK". A FlightRoute has an icaoCode for its origin airport.
identifier: identifier represents any kind of identifier (e.g., ISBN, GTIN, UUID) for a Thing, as a PropertyValue, Text, or URL. Also called "ID", "unique code", "reference number". Examples: A Product has an identifier "ISBN 978-0321765723". A Person has an identifier "UUID:123-abc". A Thing has an identifier a PropertyValue for a custom ID.
identifyingExam: identifyingExam specifies a PhysicalExam that can identify a MedicalSign. Also called "diagnostic exam", "confirmatory exam". Examples: A MedicalSign has an identifyingExam "Neurological Exam". A Symptom has an identifyingExam "Physical Assessment".
identifyingTest: identifyingTest specifies a MedicalTest that can identify a MedicalSign. Also called "diagnostic test", "confirmatory test". Examples: A MedicalSign has an identifyingTest "Blood Test". A Symptom has an identifyingTest "MRI Scan".
illustrator: illustrator identifies the Person who created the illustrations for a Book. Also called "book artist", "graphic artist". Examples: A Book has an illustrator "John Doe". A ChildrensBook has an illustrator "Jane Smith".
image: image provides an ImageObject or URL representing an image of the item. Also called "item picture", "visual representation", "photo". Examples: A Product has an image "https://example.com/product.jpg". A Person has an image of their portrait. A Thing has an image as an ImageObject.
imagingTechnique: imagingTechnique specifies the MedicalImagingTechnique used in an ImagingTest. Also called "imaging method", "scan technique". Examples: An ImagingTest has an imagingTechnique "MRI". A DiagnosticScan has an imagingTechnique "CT Scan".
inAlbum: inAlbum indicates the MusicAlbum to which a MusicRecording belongs. Also called "part of album", "album track". Examples: A MusicRecording is inAlbum "Thriller". A Song is inAlbum "The Dark Side of the Moon".
inBroadcastLineup: inBroadcastLineup specifies the CableOrSatelliteService that offers a BroadcastChannel. Also called "channel lineup", "service provider". Examples: A BroadcastChannel is inBroadcastLineup "Comcast Cable". A TVChannel is inBroadcastLineup "Sky Satellite".
inChI: inChI provides the Non-proprietary identifier for a MolecularEntity, enabling linking of diverse data compilations. Also called "International Chemical Identifier", "chemical ID". Examples: A MolecularEntity has an inChI "InChI=1S/C6H12O6/c7-1-2(8)3(9)4(10)5(11)6(12)13/h2-13H,1H2". A ChemicalCompound has an inChI string.
inChIKey: inChIKey provides the hashed version (SHA-256) of the full InChI for a MolecularEntity. Also called "InChI hash", "chemical key". Examples: A MolecularEntity has an inChIKey "HEFNNWSXXYFETF-UHFFFAOYSA-N". A ChemicalCompound has an inChIKey for quick lookup.
inCodeSet: inCodeSet specifies a CategoryCodeSet that contains this CategoryCode. Also called "part of code set", "belongs to code set". Examples: A CategoryCode is inCodeSet "UNSPSC". A MedicalCode is inCodeSet "ICD-10". Distinct from `hasCategoryCode`, which indicates the reverse relationship (a code set contains a code).
inDefinedTermSet: inDefinedTermSet specifies a DefinedTermSet that contains this DefinedTerm. Also called "part of term set", "belongs to term set". Examples: A DefinedTerm is inDefinedTermSet "Schema.org Health & Life Sciences". A MedicalTerm is inDefinedTermSet "SNOMED CT". Distinct from `hasDefinedTerm`, which indicates the reverse relationship (a term set contains a term).
inLanguage: inLanguage specifies the Language of the content, performance, or action, using IETF BCP 47 standard codes. Also called "language of content", "spoken language", "written in". Examples: A CreativeWork is inLanguage "en-US". A BroadcastService is inLanguage "fr". A CommunicateAction is inLanguage "es".
inPlaylist: inPlaylist indicates the MusicPlaylist to which a MusicRecording belongs. Also called "part of playlist", "playlist track". Examples: A MusicRecording is inPlaylist "My Favorites". A Song is inPlaylist "Workout Mix".
inProductGroupWithID: inProductGroupWithID indicates the productGroupID for a ProductGroup that this Product is a variant of. Also called "product group ID", "variant group ID". Examples: A Product has an inProductGroupWithID "PG12345". A T-shirt (variant) has an inProductGroupWithID for its main product group.
inStoreReturnsOffered: inStoreReturnsOffered indicates whether in-store returns are offered as part of a MerchantReturnPolicy. Also called "in-store returns available", "physical store returns". Examples: A MerchantReturnPolicy has inStoreReturnsOffered true. A ReturnPolicy has inStoreReturnsOffered false.
inSupportOf: inSupportOf specifies the qualification, candidature, degree, or application that a Thesis supports. Also called "thesis for", "supports degree". Examples: A Thesis is inSupportOf "PhD in Physics". A Dissertation is inSupportOf "Master's Degree".
incentiveAmount: incentiveAmount describes the amount that can be redeemed from a FinancialIncentive, using LoanOrCredit, QuantitativeValue, or UnitPriceSpecification. Also called "incentive value", "rebate amount", "credit value". Examples: A FinancialIncentive has an incentiveAmount of a QuantitativeValue "$2500". An Incentive has an incentiveAmount as a LoanOrCredit. A Rebate has an incentiveAmount as a UnitPriceSpecification.
incentiveCompensation: incentiveCompensation describes the bonus and commission compensation aspects of a JobPosting. Also called "bonus structure", "commission details", "performance pay". Examples: A JobPosting has incentiveCompensation "Quarterly bonuses based on performance". A SalesJob has incentiveCompensation "10% commission on sales".
incentiveStatus: incentiveStatus specifies the IncentiveStatus (e.g., active, on hold, retired) of a FinancialIncentive. Also called "incentive state", "status of incentive". Examples: A FinancialIncentive has an incentiveStatus "Active". An Incentive has an incentiveStatus "On Hold".
incentiveType: incentiveType specifies the type of incentive offered (e.g., tax credit/rebate, tax deduction, subsidy) by a FinancialIncentive. Also called "type of rebate", "subsidy type", "credit type". Examples: A FinancialIncentive has an incentiveType "Tax Credit". An Incentive has an incentiveType "Rebate".
incentives: incentives describes the bonus and commission compensation aspects of a JobPosting. Also called "bonus structure", "commission details", "performance pay". Examples: A JobPosting has incentives "Annual performance bonus". A SalesRole has incentives "Uncapped commission". Distinct from `incentiveCompensation`, which is a more specific property for the same concept.
incentivizedItem: incentivizedItem specifies the DefinedTerm (product/service category) or Product (specific product/service) that is being incentivized by a FinancialIncentive. Also called "eligible item", "covered product", "incentive target". Examples: A FinancialIncentive has an incentivizedItem a DefinedTerm for "Photovoltaic module". An Incentive has an incentivizedItem a Product "Energy Efficient Refrigerator".
includedComposition: includedComposition specifies smaller MusicComposition(s) that are included within a larger MusicComposition, such as a movement in a symphony. Also called "part of composition", "contains movement". Examples: A Symphony has an includedComposition "First Movement". A Suite has an includedComposition "Prelude".
includedDataCatalog: includedDataCatalog specifies a DataCatalog which contains this Dataset. Also called "part of data catalog", "dataset catalog". Examples: A Dataset is includedDataCatalog "Government Open Data Portal". A ResearchDataset is includedDataCatalog "University Data Repository". Distinct from `includedInDataCatalog`, which is the preferred name for this property.
includedInDataCatalog: includedInDataCatalog specifies a DataCatalog which contains this Dataset. Also called "part of data catalog", "dataset catalog". Examples: A Dataset is includedInDataCatalog "Government Open Data Portal". A ResearchDataset is includedInDataCatalog "University Data Repository". Distinct from `includedDataCatalog`, which is an older name for this property.
includedInHealthInsurancePlan: includedInHealthInsurancePlan indicates the HealthInsurancePlan(s) that cover a specific Drug. Also called "drug covered by plan", "insurance coverage". Examples: A Drug is includedInHealthInsurancePlan "Blue Cross PPO". A Medication is includedInHealthInsurancePlan "Medicare Part D".
includedRiskFactor: includedRiskFactor specifies a MedicalRiskFactor (modifiable or non-modifiable) that is included in the calculation of a MedicalRiskEstimator. Also called "risk factor component", "factor in risk assessment". Examples: A MedicalRiskEstimator has an includedRiskFactor "Age". A RiskAssessmentTool has an includedRiskFactor "Smoking History".
includesAttraction: includesAttraction specifies a TouristAttraction located at a TouristDestination. Also called "destination attraction", "contains attraction". Examples: A TouristDestination includesAttraction "Eiffel Tower". A City includesAttraction "Central Park".
includesHealthPlanFormulary: includesHealthPlanFormulary specifies the HealthPlanFormulary(s) covered by a HealthInsurancePlan. Also called "plan formulary", "drug list included". Examples: A HealthInsurancePlan includesHealthPlanFormulary "Preferred Drug List". An InsurancePlan includesHealthPlanFormulary "Standard Formulary".
includesHealthPlanNetwork: includesHealthPlanNetwork specifies the HealthPlanNetwork(s) covered by a HealthInsurancePlan. Also called "plan network", "provider network included". Examples: A HealthInsurancePlan includesHealthPlanNetwork "PPO Network". An InsurancePlan includesHealthPlanNetwork "HMO Network".
includesObject: An Offer, Demand, or ProductCollection includes a specific object, represented by a TypeAndQuantityNode, to indicate the exact quantity of products contained within it. Also called "contains object", "comprises item", "features product quantity". Examples: "An Offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 apples.", "A ProductCollection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 10 books.", "A Demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 tickets."
incomeLimit: A FinancialIncentive has an income limit, which is a MonetaryAmount or Text, specifying the maximum annualized income or other criteria for which the incentive is applicable. Also called "income cap", "eligibility income", "income threshold". Examples: "This FinancialIncentive has an incomeLimit of $114,000.", "The grant has an incomeLimit of '120% of median poverty income'.", "The tax credit has an incomeLimit based on household earnings."
increasesRiskOf: A MedicalRiskFactor increases the risk of a MedicalEntity, which is a condition, complication, or other medical entity influenced by this factor. Also called "predisposes to", "contributes to risk of", "heightens likelihood of". Examples: "Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer.", "High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack.", "Lack of exercise increasesRiskOf obesity."
industry: A JobPosting is associated with an industry, which is a DefinedTerm or Text describing the sector of the job position. Also called "job sector", "field of work", "business area". Examples: "This JobPosting is in the 'Technology' industry.", "The position is in the 'Healthcare' industry.", "The JobPosting specifies 'Manufacturing' as its industry."
ineligibleRegion: An ActionAccessSpecification, DeliveryChargeSpecification, Demand, MediaObject, or Offer has an ineligible region, which is a GeoShape, Place, or Text, indicating a geo-political region where the item or service is not valid or allowed. Also called "restricted region", "excluded area", "unavailable in". Examples: "This Offer has an ineligibleRegion of 'Alaska'.", "The DeliveryChargeSpecification has an ineligibleRegion defined by a GeoShape.", "The MediaObject is ineligibleRegion 'EU countries'." Distinct from `eligibleRegion`, which specifies regions where an offer or delivery charge is valid.
infectiousAgent: An InfectiousDisease is caused by an infectious agent, which is Text describing the specific pathogen. Also called "causative agent", "pathogen", "disease vector". Examples: "Influenza is caused by the infectiousAgent 'Influenza virus'.", "Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgent 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'.", "Malaria's infectiousAgent is 'Plasmodium falciparum'."
