Also called media background info, contextual details, original content description. Examples: A fact-check review has original media context description 'Video was taken out of context from a 2018 protest'. A media analysis has original media context description 'Image was digitally altered from a stock photo'. A news review has original media context description 'Quote was part of a longer speech, not a standalone statement'.
originalMediaLink: A MediaReview links to an original media link, which is a URL or MediaObject pointing to the original version of the reviewed content. Also called source media link, original content URL, link to original. Examples: A fact-check review has original media link 'https://youtube.com/originalvideo'. A media analysis has original media link 'https://example.com/originalimage.jpg'. A news review has original media link 'https://news.com/article-source'.
originatesFrom: A LymphaticVessel originates from a specific vessel, indicating the vasculature from which the lymphatic structure arises. Also called arises from, derived from, afferent from. Examples: A lymphatic vessel originates from 'capillary bed'. The thoracic duct originates from 'cisterna chyli'. A lymphatic capillary originates from 'interstitial fluid'.
overdosage: A Drug provides information on overdosage, detailing signs, symptoms, treatments, and emergency contacts for an overdose situation. Also called overdose information, toxicity details, emergency overdose guidance. Examples: Acetaminophen has overdosage 'liver damage, seek medical attention immediately'. Insulin has overdosage 'hypoglycemia, administer glucose'. A sedative has overdosage 'respiratory depression, call 911'. Distinct from adverseReaction, which describes side effects at normal doses.
ownedFrom: OwnershipInfo indicates the date and time a product was owned from, marking the start of ownership. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, ownership start date. Examples: Car ownership info has owned from '2020-01-01'. Property ownership info has owned from '2015-06-15T10:00:00Z'. A book's ownership info has owned from '1999-12-25'. Distinct from ownedThrough, which marks the end of ownership.
ownedThrough: OwnershipInfo indicates the date and time a product was owned through, marking the end of ownership. Also called disposal date, sale date, ownership end date. Examples: Car ownership info has owned through '2023-01-01'. Property ownership info has owned through '2022-03-30T17:00:00Z'. A book's ownership info has owned through '2010-05-01'. Distinct from ownedFrom, which marks the start of ownership.
owner: A Thing is possessed by an owner, who is the Person or Organization holding legal title or rights to it. Also called possessed by, belongs to, proprietor. Examples: A house has owner 'John Doe'. A car has owner 'Acme Rentals'. A patent has owner 'Innovate Corp'. Distinct from creator, who made the item.
ownershipFundingInfo: A NewsMediaOrganization or Organization provides ownership funding info, which describes its ownership structure, funding sources, and grants, especially concerning editorial independence. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure details, financial backing information. Examples: A news organization has ownership funding info 'Owned by a non-profit foundation, funded by public grants'. A media company has ownership funding info 'Publicly traded, funded by advertising revenue'. A research institute has ownership funding info 'Funded by government grants and private donations'. Distinct from funder, which is a specific entity providing funds.
owns: An Organization or Person owns a specific thing, indicating possession or legal title over it. Also called possesses, has title to, is proprietor of. Examples: John Doe owns 'a house'. Acme Corp owns 'several patents'. The museum owns 'a collection of artifacts'. Distinct from owner, which is the inverse property.
pageEnd: An Article, Chapter, or Publication ends on a specific page end, which is the final page number of the work. Also called ending page, last page, final page number. Examples: An article has page end '138'. A chapter has page end 'xvi'. A journal paper has page end '25'. Distinct from pageStart, which is the beginning page number.
pageStart: An Article, Chapter, or Publication starts on a specific page start, which is the initial page number of the work. Also called starting page, first page, initial page number. Examples: An article has page start '135'. A chapter has page start 'xiii'. A journal paper has page start '10'. Distinct from pageEnd, which is the ending page number.
pagination: An Article, Chapter, or Publication has pagination, which is a free-form textual description of its page numbers, not separated into start and end. Also called page range, page numbering, page description. Examples: An article has pagination '1-6, 9, 55'. A chapter has pagination '10-12, 46-49'. A journal paper has pagination 'pp. 78-85'. Distinct from pageStart and pageEnd, which are specific start and end page numbers.
parent: A Person has a parent, who is an individual from whom they are descended. Also called is child of, mother, father. Examples: Alice has parent 'Bob'. John has parent 'Mary'. A child has parent 'their biological mother'. Distinct from children, which is the inverse property.
parentItem: A parentItem is the Comment or CreativeWork that an Answer, Comment, or Question is a reply to or part of. Also called replied to by, part of, in response to, is a child of. Examples: A Comment parentItem an Article. An Answer parentItem a Question. A Question parentItem a CreativeWork. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.
parentOrganization: A parentOrganization is the larger Organization that a given Organization is a sub-organization of. Also called is a subsidiary of, belongs to, is part of, owned by. Examples: Google parentOrganization Alphabet Inc.. YouTube parentOrganization Google. A local branch parentOrganization the national bank. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a parent to its child organization.
parentService: A parentService is the broader BroadcastService that a specific BroadcastService is a regional variation or component of. Also called is a regional variant of, belongs to, is a component of. Examples: BBC One Scotland parentService BBC One. A local news channel parentService a national news network. A regional radio station parentService a national radio service.
parentTaxon: A parentTaxon is the immediate higher-level Taxon (or its name/URL) that a given Taxon is classified under. Also called classified under, belongs to the taxon, is a sub-taxon of. Examples: Canis lupus parentTaxon Canis. Homo sapiens parentTaxon Homo. Felidae parentTaxon Carnivora.
parents: parents are the Person entities who are the biological or adoptive parents of another Person. Also called is a child of, gave birth to, raised by. Examples: Alice parents Bob. Charlie parents Diana. Eve parents Frank and Grace. Distinct from children, which points from a parent to their child.
partOfEpisode: partOfEpisode is the Episode that a specific Clip is a segment or portion of. Also called is a segment of, belongs to episode, featured in episode. Examples: A movie trailer partOfEpisode the full movie episode. A highlight reel partOfEpisode a sports broadcast episode. A deleted scene partOfEpisode a TV show episode.
partOfInvoice: partOfInvoice is the Invoice that an Order is included in for payment. Also called included in invoice, billed on invoice, paid via invoice. Examples: Order #123 partOfInvoice Invoice #ABC. A purchase order partOfInvoice a monthly billing statement. A service request partOfInvoice a consolidated invoice.
partOfOrder: partOfOrder is the overarching Order that a ParcelDelivery is a component of. Also called belongs to order, is a delivery for order, included in order. Examples: Delivery #XYZ partOfOrder Order #456. A package shipment partOfOrder a customer's online purchase. A food delivery partOfOrder a restaurant order.
partOfSeason: partOfSeason is the CreativeWorkSeason that an Episode or Clip belongs to. Also called belongs to season, is in season, featured in season. Examples: Episode 5 partOfSeason Season 1. A blooper reel partOfSeason the final season of a show. A specific scene partOfSeason the second season of a drama.
partOfSeries: partOfSeries is the CreativeWorkSeries that a Clip, CreativeWorkSeason, or Episode belongs to. Also called belongs to series, is in series, featured in series. Examples: Season 3 partOfSeries Game of Thrones. Episode 10 partOfSeries The Mandalorian. A short clip partOfSeries a documentary series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TVSeries.
partOfSystem: partOfSystem is the AnatomicalSystem that an AnatomicalStructure is a component of. Also called belongs to system, is a component of, forms part of system. Examples: The heart partOfSystem the circulatory system. The lungs partOfSystem the respiratory system. The femur partOfSystem the skeletal system.
partOfTVSeries: partOfTVSeries is the TVSeries that a TVClip, TVEpisode, or TVSeason belongs to. Also called belongs to TV series, is in TV series, featured in TV series. Examples: Season 5 of Friends partOfTVSeries Friends. The pilot episode partOfTVSeries The Office. A deleted scene from a TV show partOfTVSeries its respective TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any CreativeWorkSeries.
partOfTrip: partOfTrip is the larger Trip that a specific Trip is a sub-component or segment of. Also called is a segment of trip, belongs to trip, is a sub-trip of. Examples: Day 1 of vacation partOfTrip the entire vacation. The hiking portion partOfTrip the adventure tour. The flight segment partOfTrip the business travel.
participant: A participant is an Organization or Person who indirectly took part in an Action alongside the main agent. Also called co-agent, involved in, assisted by, collaborated with. Examples: A writing action participant a co-author. A meeting participant an attendee. A project participant a team member. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of the action.
partySize: partySize is the Integer or QuantitativeValue representing the number of people a FoodEstablishmentReservation or TaxiReservation is intended to accommodate. Also called number of guests, group size, capacity for. Examples: A dinner reservation partySize 4. A taxi booking partySize 3. A table booking partySize a value of 6.
passengerPriorityStatus: passengerPriorityStatus is the QualitativeValue or Text indicating the priority level assigned to a passenger for a FlightReservation, typically for security or boarding. Also called boarding priority, security status, priority level. Examples: A flight reservation passengerPriorityStatus "FastTrack". A flight reservation passengerPriorityStatus "Priority Boarding". A flight reservation passengerPriorityStatus "Elite Status".
passengerSequenceNumber: passengerSequenceNumber is the Text identifier assigned by the airline to a passenger for a FlightReservation, indicating their sequence in a process. Also called boarding sequence, check-in number, airline sequence ID. Examples: A flight reservation passengerSequenceNumber "001". A flight reservation passengerSequenceNumber "A12". A flight reservation passengerSequenceNumber "F03".
pathophysiology: pathophysiology is the Text description of the functional changes in the body's normal processes associated with a MedicalCondition or PhysicalActivity. Also called disease mechanism, functional changes, biological impact. Examples: Diabetes pathophysiology insulin resistance and impaired glucose metabolism. Hypertension pathophysiology increased vascular resistance and cardiac output. Running pathophysiology increased heart rate and muscle oxygen consumption.
pattern: pattern is the DefinedTerm or Text describing the decorative or structural design of a CreativeWork or Product. Also called design, motif, print, style. Examples: A shirt pattern "striped". A wallpaper pattern "floral". A blanket pattern "plaid".
payload: payload is the QuantitativeValue representing the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo that a Vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, maximum cargo weight. Examples: A truck payload 1000 kg. A car payload 500 lbs. An airplane payload 20 tons.
paymentAccepted: paymentAccepted is the Text indicating the types of payment methods that a LocalBusiness accepts. Also called accepts payment by, payment options, payment methods. Examples: A restaurant paymentAccepted "Credit Card". A store paymentAccepted "Cash". An online shop paymentAccepted "PayPal".
paymentDue: paymentDue is the DateTime by which payment for an Invoice or Order is required. Also called due date, payment deadline, payment required by. Examples: An invoice paymentDue 2023-12-31. An order paymentDue next Friday. A bill paymentDue 2024-01-15T17:00:00. Distinct from paymentDueDate, which is a similar property but can also be a Date type.
paymentDueDate: paymentDueDate is the Date or DateTime by which payment for an Invoice or Order is required. Also called due date, payment deadline, payment required by. Examples: An invoice paymentDueDate 2023-12-31. An order paymentDueDate next Friday. A bill paymentDueDate 2024-01-15T17:00:00. Distinct from paymentDue, which is a similar property but specifically DateTime.
paymentMethod: paymentMethod is the PaymentMethod or Text describing how an Invoice or Order was or will be paid. Also called method of payment, payment type, paid by. Examples: An order paymentMethod "Visa". An invoice paymentMethod "Bank Transfer". A purchase paymentMethod PaymentMethod.PayPal.
paymentMethodId: paymentMethodId is the Text identifier associated with the paymentMethod used for an Invoice or Order, such as the last four digits of a credit card. Also called payment ID, transaction ID, payment reference. Examples: An invoice paymentMethodId "1234". An order paymentMethodId "XYZ789". A payment record paymentMethodId "5678".
paymentMethodType: paymentMethodType is the PaymentMethodType that categorizes a specific PaymentMethod. Also called category of payment, payment classification. Examples: A credit card paymentMethodType CreditCard. A bank transfer paymentMethodType BankTransfer. A digital wallet paymentMethodType DigitalWallet.
paymentStatus: paymentStatus is the PaymentStatusType or Text indicating the current state of payment for an Invoice. Also called invoice status, payment condition, paid status. Examples: An invoice paymentStatus PaymentComplete. An invoice paymentStatus "Partially Paid". An invoice paymentStatus PaymentDue.
paymentUrl: paymentUrl is the URL where payment for an Order can be submitted. Also called payment link, pay here, submit payment at. Examples: An order paymentUrl https://example.com/pay/order123. A bill paymentUrl https://billing.company.com/invoice/XYZ. A purchase paymentUrl https://checkout.store.com/pay.
penciler: A penciler is the Person responsible for drawing the primary narrative artwork in a ComicIssue, ComicStory, or VisualArtwork. Also called artist, illustrator, sketch artist, draws by. Examples: A comic book penciler Jim Lee. A graphic novel penciler Frank Miller. A comic story penciler Jack Kirby. Distinct from inker, who applies ink over the penciler's lines, and colorist, who adds color.
percentile10: percentile10 is the Number representing the value below which 10% of the observations fall within a QuantitativeValueDistribution. Also called 10th percentage point, 10% mark. Examples: A salary distribution percentile10 30000. A test score distribution percentile10 65. A response time distribution percentile10 0.5.
percentile25: percentile25 is the Number representing the value below which 25% of the observations fall within a QuantitativeValueDistribution. Also called 25th percentage point, first quartile, 25% mark. Examples: A salary distribution percentile25 40000. A test score distribution percentile25 72. A response time distribution percentile25 1.2.
percentile75: percentile75 is the Number representing the value below which 75% of the observations fall within a QuantitativeValueDistribution. Also called 75th percentage point, third quartile, 75% mark. Examples: A salary distribution percentile75 80000. A test score distribution percentile75 90. A response time distribution percentile75 5.8.
percentile90: percentile90 is the Number representing the value below which 90% of the observations fall within a QuantitativeValueDistribution. Also called 90th percentage point, 90% mark. Examples: A salary distribution percentile90 120000. A test score distribution percentile90 95. A response time distribution percentile90 10.1.
performTime: performTime is the Duration required to execute the instructions or a direction within a HowTo guide, excluding preparation time. Also called execution time, active time, task duration. Examples: A recipe performTime PT30M (30 minutes). An assembly guide performTime PT2H (2 hours). A DIY project performTime P1D (1 day). Distinct from prepTime, which is the time taken to prepare supplies.
performer: A performer is an Organization or Person who presents or entertains at an Event. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, plays at. Examples: A concert performer a band. A conference performer a keynote speaker. A play performer an actor. Distinct from organizer, who arranges the event, and attendee, who observes.
performerIn: performerIn is an Event in which a Person acts as a performer or participant. Also called performs in, participates in, appears in. Examples: A musician performerIn a music festival. An actor performerIn a theatrical production. A speaker performerIn a public lecture. Distinct from performer, which points from the event to the person.
performers: performers are the primary Organization or Person entities who present or entertain at an Event. Also called main artists, headliners, featured performers. Examples: A concert performers The Rolling Stones. A play performers the lead actors. A festival performers multiple bands. Distinct from performer, which is singular, while performers implies multiple or the main ones.
permissionType: permissionType is the DigitalDocumentPermissionType that specifies the kind of access or action granted by a DigitalDocumentPermission. Also called access type, authorization type, rights granted. Examples: A document permission permissionType ReadPermission. A document permission permissionType WritePermission. A document permission permissionType SharePermission.
permissions: permissions is the Text describing the access rights or system capabilities a SoftwareApplication requires to function. Also called required access, app rights, system access. Examples: A mobile app permissions "Internet access". A game permissions "Storage access". A utility app permissions "Location services".
permitAudience: permitAudience is the Audience for whom a Permit is intended or valid. Also called target group, valid for, intended for. Examples: A fishing permit permitAudience anglers. A building permit permitAudience contractors. A driver's license permitAudience licensed drivers.
permittedUsage: permittedUsage is the Text detailing the allowed activities or restrictions for an Accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: A hotel room permittedUsage "No smoking". A vacation rental permittedUsage "Family use only". An apartment permittedUsage "Residential use".
petsAllowed: petsAllowed is a Boolean or Text indicating whether an Accommodation, ApartmentComplex, FloorPlan, or LodgingBusiness permits pets. Also called pet-friendly, allows animals, animal policy. Examples: A hotel petsAllowed true. An apartment complex petsAllowed "Small dogs only". A vacation rental petsAllowed false.
phoneticText: phoneticText is the Text representation of a PronounceableText using a phonetic transcription system, such as IPA. Also called phonetic transcription, pronunciation guide, IPA representation. Examples: The word "hello" phoneticText həˈloʊ. The city "London" phoneticText ˈlʌndən. A name phoneticText [ˈdʒoʊnəθən].
photo: photo is an ImageObject or Photograph depicting a Place. Also called image of, picture of, visual representation of. Examples: A restaurant photo a picture of its interior. A park photo a landscape photograph. A landmark photo an iconic image. Distinct from photos, which is used for multiple images.
photos: photos are ImageObjects or Photographs depicting a Place. Also called images of, pictures of, visual representations of. Examples: A hotel photos multiple images of rooms and facilities. A museum photos pictures of its exhibits. A city photos various scenic photographs. Distinct from photo, which is used for a single image.
physicalRequirement: physicalRequirement is a DefinedTerm, Text, or URL describing the physical activities or abilities necessary for a JobPosting. Also called physical demands, fitness requirements, required physical ability. Examples: A construction job physicalRequirement "ability to lift 50 lbs". A nursing position physicalRequirement "standing for long periods". A delivery driver job physicalRequirement "valid driver's license".
physiologicalBenefits: physiologicalBenefits is the Text describing the specific health advantages or bodily improvements associated with a Diet. Also called health benefits, bodily advantages, physical gains. Examples: A low-carb diet physiologicalBenefits "weight loss and improved blood sugar control". A Mediterranean diet physiologicalBenefits "reduced risk of heart disease". A vegan diet physiologicalBenefits "lower cholesterol levels".
pickupLocation: pickupLocation is the Place where a passenger will be collected by a TaxiReservation or where a RentalCarReservation vehicle can be obtained. Also called collection point, pick-up spot, embarkation point. Examples: A taxi reservation pickupLocation the airport terminal. A rental car reservation pickupLocation the downtown office. A ride-share booking pickupLocation the user's current address.
pickupTime: pickupTime is the DateTime when a passenger will be collected by a TaxiReservation or when a RentalCarReservation vehicle can be obtained. Also called collection time, pick-up time, embarkation time. Examples: A taxi reservation pickupTime 2023-12-25T10:00:00. A rental car reservation pickupTime tomorrow at 9 AM. A ride-share booking pickupTime now.
playMode: playMode is the GamePlayMode indicating whether a VideoGame or VideoGameSeries supports single-player, multi-player, or co-operative gameplay. Also called game mode, player mode, gameplay style. Examples: A video game playMode SinglePlayer. A video game playMode MultiPlayer. A video game playMode CoOp.
playerType: playerType is the Text specifying the software or plugin required to play a MediaObject. Also called required player, media player, playback software. Examples: A video file playerType "Flash". An audio stream playerType "HTML5 Audio". A game playerType "Unity Web Player".
playersOnline: playersOnline is the Integer representing the current number of players connected to a GameServer. Also called active players, current players, online count. Examples: A game server playersOnline 150. A multiplayer server playersOnline 5000. A private server playersOnline 10.
polygon: polygon is the Text representation of a closed geographical area defined by a series of connected, space-delimited points for a GeoShape. Also called geographical boundary, area coordinates, shape definition. Examples: A geographical region polygon "30 10, 40 40, 20 40, 10 20, 30 10". A property boundary polygon "lat1 lon1, lat2 lon2, lat3 lon3, lat1 lon1". A city district polygon "40.71 -74.01, 40.72 -73.99, 40.70 -73.98, 40.71 -74.01".
populationType: populationType is the Class that defines the common characteristics of all members within a StatisticalPopulation or all cases within a StatisticalVariable. Also called demographic group, target population, study group. Examples: A statistical population populationType Person. A statistical variable populationType Patient. A study group populationType Organization.
position: position is the Integer or Text indicating the sequential order of a CreativeWork or ListItem within a series. Also called order in sequence, rank, index. Examples: A book chapter position 5. A list item position "first". A search result position 1.
positiveNotes: positiveNotes is an ItemList, ListItem, Text, or WebContent detailing favorable aspects or highlights of a Product or Review. Also called pros, advantages, highlights, good points. Examples: A product review positiveNotes "Excellent battery life". A product positiveNotes ["Sleek design", "User-friendly interface"]. A service review positiveNotes a list of positive feedback. Distinct from negativeNotes, which describes unfavorable aspects.
possibleComplication: possibleComplication is the Text describing a potential unexpected and adverse development or outcome of a MedicalCondition. Also called potential risk, adverse event, secondary condition. Examples: Diabetes possibleComplication "kidney failure". Surgery possibleComplication "infection". Influenza possibleComplication "pneumonia".
possibleTreatment: possibleTreatment is a Drug, DrugClass, LifestyleModification, or MedicalTherapy that may be used to address a MedicalCondition or MedicalSignOrSymptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention for. Examples: Headache possibleTreatment Ibuprofen. High blood pressure possibleTreatment LifestyleModification. Anxiety possibleTreatment Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.
postOfficeBoxNumber: postOfficeBoxNumber is the Text representing the P.O. Box number within a PostalAddress. Also called PO box, mailbox number. Examples: A postal address postOfficeBoxNumber "12345". A business address postOfficeBoxNumber "P.O. Box 789". A mailing address postOfficeBoxNumber "Box 500".
postOp: postOp is the Text describing the care, procedures, and follow-ups required after the use or implantation of a MedicalDevice. Also called postoperative care, aftercare, recovery instructions. Examples: A surgical implant postOp "regular check-ups and physical therapy". A medical device postOp "monitor for signs of infection". A prosthetic limb postOp "fitting adjustments and rehabilitation". Distinct from preOp, which describes preparations before a procedure.
postalCode: postalCode is the Text representing the postal code for a DefinedRegion, GeoCoordinates, GeoShape, or PostalAddress. Also called zip code, postcode, area code. Examples: A postal address postalCode "90210". Geo-coordinates postalCode "SW1A 0AA". A defined region postalCode "10001".
postalCodeBegin: postalCodeBegin is the Text representing the starting postal code (inclusive) of a range defined by a PostalCodeRangeSpecification. Also called range start postal code, first zip code. Examples: A postal code range postalCodeBegin "90001". A delivery zone postalCodeBegin "SW1A". A service area postalCodeBegin "10000". Distinct from postalCodeEnd, which is the ending postal code in a range.
postalCodeEnd: postalCodeEnd is the Text representing the ending postal code (inclusive) of a range defined by a PostalCodeRangeSpecification. Also called range end postal code, last zip code. Examples: A postal code range postalCodeEnd "90099". A delivery zone postalCodeEnd "SW1Z". A service area postalCodeEnd "10099". Distinct from postalCodeBegin, which is the starting postal code in a range.
postalCodePrefix: postalCodePrefix is the Text representing a common prefix that defines a range of postal codes within a DefinedRegion, often used in non-numeric systems. Also called zip code prefix, postcode area, regional postal code. Examples: A defined region postalCodePrefix "SW1A". A delivery area postalCodePrefix "N1". A service zone postalCodePrefix "EC2". Distinct from postalCodeRange, which specifies a full range object.
postalCodeRange: postalCodeRange is a PostalCodeRangeSpecification that defines a range of postal codes for a DefinedRegion. Also called zip code range, postcode range, service area by postal code. Examples: A delivery region postalCodeRange a specification for 90001-90099. A sales territory postalCodeRange a range covering multiple zip codes. A service area postalCodeRange a specification for a specific postcode range. Distinct from postalCodePrefix, which is a textual prefix, not a full range object.
potentialAction: potentialAction is an Action that could ideally be performed with a Thing as its object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A book potentialAction ReadAction. A product potentialAction BuyAction. A person potentialAction CallAction.
potentialUse: potentialUse is a DefinedTerm describing the intended human application or purpose of a ChemicalSubstance or MolecularEntity. Also called intended application, possible purpose, human use. Examples: A chemical substance potentialUse as a cleaning agent. A molecular entity potentialUse in drug development. A compound potentialUse as a food additive.
practicesAt: practicesAt is the MedicalOrganization where an IndividualPhysician performs their medical duties. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by. Examples: Dr. Smith practicesAt General Hospital. A pediatrician practicesAt Children's Clinic. A surgeon practicesAt St. Jude's Medical Center.
preOp: preOp is the Text describing the preparations, tests, and procedures required before the use or implantation of a MedicalDevice. Also called preoperative instructions, pre-procedure care, readiness steps. Examples: A surgical implant preOp "blood tests and imaging scans". A medical device preOp "patient education and consent". A diagnostic tool preOp "fasting for 8 hours". Distinct from postOp, which describes care after a procedure.
predecessorOf: predecessorOf is the newer ProductModel that a previous, often discontinued, ProductModel has been replaced by or evolved into. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, evolved into. Examples: iPhone 10 predecessorOf iPhone 11. Windows XP predecessorOf Windows Vista. Model A car predecessorOf Model B car. Distinct from successorOf, which points from the newer variant to the older one.
pregnancyCategory: pregnancyCategory is the DrugPregnancyCategory assigned to a Drug, indicating its potential risks during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy risk, fetal risk category. Examples: A drug pregnancyCategory Category A. A medication pregnancyCategory Category X. A pharmaceutical pregnancyCategory Category C.
pregnancyWarning: pregnancyWarning is the Text providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding a Drug's use during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy precautions, warning for pregnant women, fetal safety information. Examples: A drug pregnancyWarning "Consult a doctor before use if pregnant". A medication pregnancyWarning "Not recommended during the first trimester". A pharmaceutical pregnancyWarning "May cause fetal harm".
prepTime: prepTime is the Duration required to prepare the necessary items or ingredients for instructions or a direction within a HowTo guide. Also called preparation duration, setup time, readiness time. Examples: A recipe prepTime PT15M (15 minutes). An assembly guide prepTime PT10M (10 minutes). A craft project prepTime PT30M (30 minutes). Distinct from performTime, which is the time taken to execute the instructions.
preparation: preparation is a MedicalEntity or Text describing the typical actions a patient must take before undergoing a MedicalProcedure. Also called patient prep, pre-procedure instructions, readiness steps. Examples: A surgery preparation "fasting from midnight". A diagnostic test preparation avoiding certain medications. A dental cleaning preparation "brushing teeth thoroughly".
prescribingInfo: prescribingInfo is the URL providing access to the official prescribing information for a Drug. Also called drug information link, medication guide, dosage instructions. Examples: A drug prescribingInfo https://www.fda.gov/drug/info/XYZ. A medication prescribingInfo a link to its package insert. A pharmaceutical prescribingInfo a URL for healthcare professionals.
prescriptionStatus: prescriptionStatus is the DrugPrescriptionStatus or Text indicating whether a Drug requires a prescription or is available over-the-counter. Also called drug availability, OTC status, prescription requirement. Examples: A drug prescriptionStatus PrescriptionOnly. A medication prescriptionStatus OverTheCounter. A pharmaceutical prescriptionStatus "Controlled Substance".
previousItem: previousItem is the ListItem that immediately precedes the current ListItem in a sequence. Also called precedes, comes before, earlier item. Examples: Item B previousItem Item A. The second step previousItem the first step. A page in a pagination previousItem the page before it. Distinct from nextItem, which points to the item that follows.
previousStartDate: previousStartDate is the Date or DateTime when an Event was originally scheduled to begin before being rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start time, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled concert previousStartDate 2023-03-15. A postponed meeting previousStartDate 2023-10-20T14:00:00. A cancelled festival previousStartDate June 1, 2023. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.
price: price is the Number or Text representing the monetary cost of an Offer, PriceSpecification, DonateAction, or TradeAction. Also called cost, value, rate, charge. Examples: A product offer price 19.99. A service price "Free". A price specification price 100.
priceComponent: priceComponent is a PriceSpecification that contributes to the total cost of a CompoundPriceSpecification. Also called price element, cost breakdown, sub-price. Examples: A total price priceComponent the base unit price. A service charge priceComponent a tax component. A bundled offer priceComponent the price of an add-on.
priceComponentType: priceComponentType is the PriceComponentTypeEnumeration that categorizes a specific UnitPriceSpecification as a part of an offer's total price. Also called component type, charge type, line item category. Examples: A unit price specification priceComponentType BasePrice. A tax component priceComponentType Tax. A shipping fee priceComponentType Shipping.
priceCurrency: priceCurrency is the Text (ISO 4217 format) specifying the currency in which the price of an Offer, PriceSpecification, Reservation, Ticket, DonateAction, or TradeAction is expressed. Also called currency type, monetary unit, currency code. Examples: An offer priceCurrency "USD". A ticket priceCurrency "EUR". A reservation priceCurrency "GBP".
priceRange: priceRange is the Text indicating the general cost level or affordability of a LocalBusiness. Also called cost level, affordability, price tier. Examples: A restaurant priceRange "$$". A luxury store priceRange "$$$$". A budget hotel priceRange "$".
priceSpecification: priceSpecification is a PriceSpecification providing detailed pricing information, including unit price and charges, for a Demand, DonateAction, Offer, or TradeAction. Also called detailed pricing, cost breakdown, pricing structure. Examples: An offer priceSpecification a specification for a product's price. A demand priceSpecification a pricing model. A trade action priceSpecification a detailed cost breakdown.
priceType: priceType is the PriceTypeEnumeration or Text that categorizes the nature of a price within a CompoundPriceSpecification or UnitPriceSpecification, such as a list price or sale price. Also called pricing category, cost classification, rate type. Examples: A product priceType ListPrice. A discounted price priceType SalePrice. A suggested price priceType MSRP.
priceValidUntil: priceValidUntil is the Date after which the price specified in an Offer is no longer applicable. Also called offer expiry date, price expiration, valid until. Examples: A product offer priceValidUntil 2024-01-31. A discount priceValidUntil next Sunday. A promotional price priceValidUntil 2023-12-25.
primaryImageOfPage: primaryImageOfPage is the main ImageObject featured on a WebPage. Also called main image, featured image, hero image. Examples: A blog post primaryImageOfPage its featured header image. A product page primaryImageOfPage the main product photo. A news article primaryImageOfPage the lead image. Distinct from image, which can be any image on the page.
primaryPrevention: primaryPrevention is a MedicalTherapy aimed at preventing the initial onset of a MedicalCondition. Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, first-line prevention. Examples: Influenza primaryPrevention vaccination. Heart disease primaryPrevention healthy diet and exercise. Dental cavities primaryPrevention fluoride treatment. Distinct from secondaryPrevention, which aims to detect and treat early, and tertiaryPrevention, which manages existing conditions.
printColumn: printColumn is the Text indicating the column number where a NewsArticle is located in its print edition. Also called column number, print layout column. Examples: A news article printColumn "3". A newspaper story printColumn "Column A". An editorial printColumn "2".
printEdition: printEdition is the Text specifying the particular edition of a print product in which a NewsArticle was published. Also called newspaper edition, magazine edition, print version. Examples: A news article printEdition "Late City Edition". A newspaper story printEdition "Morning Edition". An article printEdition "National Edition".
printPage: printPage is the Text indicating the exact page name (e.g., "A5") where a NewsArticle can be found in its print publication. Also called page number, print location, article page. Examples: A news article printPage "A12". A newspaper story printPage "B3". An editorial printPage "Op-Ed 1".
printSection: printSection is the Text indicating the specific section of a print publication where a NewsArticle appeared. Also called newspaper section, magazine section, print category. Examples: A news article printSection "Sports". A newspaper story printSection "Business". An editorial printSection "Opinion".
procedure: procedure is the Text describing the steps for setting up, using, or installing a MedicalDevice. Also called usage instructions, installation guide, operational steps. Examples: A medical device procedure "Insert catheter into vein". A diagnostic machine procedure "Follow on-screen prompts for calibration". A surgical tool procedure "Sterilize before each use".
procedureType: procedureType is the MedicalProcedureType that categorizes a MedicalProcedure, such as surgical or non-invasive. Also called procedure category, medical intervention type. Examples: A surgery procedureType SurgicalProcedure. An MRI scan procedureType NoninvasiveProcedure. A biopsy procedureType PercutaneousProcedure.
processingTime: processingTime is the Duration representing the estimated time required to complete a service when accessed through a specific ServiceChannel. Also called service duration, handling time, turnaround time. Examples: An online application channel processingTime P3D (3 days). A customer service hotline processingTime PT10M (10 minutes). A document submission portal processingTime P1W (1 week).
processorRequirements: processorRequirements is the Text specifying the necessary processor architecture (e.g., "x86", "ARM") for a SoftwareApplication to run. Also called CPU requirements, architecture compatibility, processor type. Examples: A software application processorRequirements "x64". A mobile app processorRequirements "ARM". A legacy program processorRequirements "IA64".
producer: A producer is the Organization or Person responsible for overseeing the creation and production of a CreativeWork, such as a movie or music album. Also called made by, created by, executive producer, production company. Examples: A movie producer Steven Spielberg. A music album producer Columbia Records. A TV series producer Shonda Rhimes. Distinct from director, who guides the artistic and dramatic aspects, and creator, who originates the work.
produces: produces is the Thing that is the tangible outcome or output generated by a Service. Also called generates, yields, results in, creates. Examples: A passport application service produces a passport. A permit application service produces a building permit. A printing service produces printed documents.
productGroupID: productGroupID is the Text identifier assigned to a ProductGroup. Also called group ID, product category ID, collection ID. Examples: A product group productGroupID "Electronics_Smartphones". A clothing line productGroupID "SummerCollection2023". A software suite productGroupID "OfficeSuitePro".
productID: productID is the Text identifier, such as an ISBN or GTIN, uniquely associated with a Product. Also called item ID, unique identifier, product code. Examples: A book productID "isbn:978-0321765723". A consumer good productID "gtin13:0123456789012". A software license productID "SKU-XYZ-789".
productSupported: A ContactPoint provides support for a specific Product or general category of products/services. Also called 'supports product', 'provides support for', 'related to product'. Examples: 'A customer service hotline supports the iPhone 15 Pro.' 'The technical support email addresses smartphones.' 'The help desk contact point supports Microsoft Office Suite.'
productionCompany: A CreativeWork (like a movie or TV series) is produced by an Organization (production company or studio). Also called 'produced by', 'made by', 'studio behind', 'created by'. Examples: 'The Matrix was produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.' 'Game of Thrones was produced by HBO Entertainment.' 'Cyberpunk 2077 was produced by CD Projekt Red.'
productionDate: A Product or Vehicle was manufactured or created on a specific Date. Also called 'manufactured on', 'made on', 'created on'. Examples: 'The car's production date was 2023-01-15.' 'This model of smartphone has a production date of 2022-10-01.' 'The vintage bicycle has a production date of 1975-03-20.'
proficiencyLevel: A TechArticle requires a certain Text-based proficiency level to understand or apply its content. Also called 'skill level required', 'expertise needed'. Examples: 'This programming guide requires a proficiency level of Expert.' 'The tutorial has a proficiency level of Beginner.' 'The advanced article targets an Expert proficiency level.'
program: A ProgramMembership is associated with a specific MemberProgram. Also called 'membership program', 'part of program'. Examples: 'This loyalty membership is part of the Star Alliance program.' 'The gym membership belongs to the Platinum MemberProgram.' 'Her frequent flyer membership is associated with the SkyMiles program.'
programMembershipUsed: A Reservation utilizes a specific ProgramMembership (e.g., loyalty program) to apply benefits. Also called 'membership applied', 'benefits from membership'. Examples: 'The flight reservation used a SkyMiles program membership.' 'The hotel booking applied a Hilton Honors program membership.' 'The car rental reservation utilized an Avis Preferred program membership.'
programName: A ProgramMembership is identified by a Text-based name of the program. Also called 'name of program', 'program title'. Examples: 'The program name for this membership is 'Gold Tier Rewards'.' 'Her membership has the program name 'Frequent Flyer Plus'.' 'The gym membership's program name is 'Premium Access'.' Distinct from program, which links to a structured MemberProgram object.
programPrerequisites: An EducationalOccupationalProgram requires certain prerequisites, which can be an AlignmentObject, Course, EducationalOccupationalCredential, or Text. Also called 'entry requirements', 'required background', 'prior learning'. Examples: 'The master's program requires a Bachelor's degree as a prerequisite.' 'This course has program prerequisites of 'Introduction to Algebra'.' 'Enrollment in the program requires a 'Level 1 Certification'.' 'The program prerequisites include 'basic computer literacy'.'
programType: An EducationalOccupationalProgram is categorized by a DefinedTerm or Text describing its type. Also called 'kind of program', 'program category'. Examples: 'The program type is 'internship'.' 'This is a 'classroom' program type.' 'The program type is 'alternance'.' 'The program type is 'online course'.'
programmingLanguage: SoftwareSourceCode is written in a specific ComputerLanguage or Text-based programming language. Also called 'language used', 'coded in'. Examples: 'The software is written in the programming language 'Python'.' 'The application uses 'Java' as its programming language.' 'The script's programming language is 'JavaScript'.'
programmingModel: An APIReference indicates whether its programming model is managed or unmanaged, described by Text. Also called 'API model type'. Examples: 'The API reference specifies a programming model of 'managed'.' 'This API uses an 'unmanaged' programming model.'
pronouns: A Person uses specific DefinedTerm, StructuredValue, or Text to describe their pronouns. Also called 'personal pronouns', 'gender pronouns'. Examples: 'Her pronouns are 'she/her'.' 'Their pronouns are 'they/them'.' 'The person's pronouns are 'he/him'.' 'The pronouns are described as 'ze/zir'.' 'The pronouns are 'any'.' 'The pronouns are 'ask me'.'
propertyID: A PropertyValue is identified by a Text or URL, often a standard code or site-specific identifier. Also called 'identifier for property', 'property code'. Examples: 'The propertyID for color is 'ISO 12345-C'.' 'The propertyID is 'vendor_sku_123'.' 'The propertyID is 'https://example.com/glossary#weight'.'
proprietaryName: A DietarySupplement or Drug has a Text-based proprietary name, typically given by its originator. Also called 'brand name', 'trade name'. Examples: 'The dietary supplement has the proprietary name 'VitaBoost'.' 'The drug's proprietary name is 'PainAway'.' 'The diet plan's proprietary name is 'KetoFast'.'
proteinContent: NutritionInformation specifies the Mass of protein contained. Also called 'amount of protein', 'protein per serving'. Examples: 'The nutrition information lists protein content as 20 grams.' 'This food has a protein content of 15g.' 'The protein content is 50 mg.'
provider: An Action, CreativeWork, Program, Invoice, ParcelDelivery, Reservation, Service, or Trip is performed or offered by an Organization or Person. Also called 'offered by', 'performed by', 'supplied by', 'seller'. Examples: 'The service is provided by 'Acme Corp'.' 'The reservation was made through 'Booking.com'.' 'The parcel delivery is handled by 'FedEx'.' 'The educational program is provided by 'University of XYZ'.' 'The invoice was issued by 'Global Services Inc.'.'
providerMobility: A Service indicates its mobility as Text (e.g., 'static' or 'dynamic'). Also called 'service mobility type'. Examples: 'The service has a provider mobility of 'static'.' 'The delivery service's provider mobility is 'dynamic'.' 'The repair service has 'mobile' provider mobility.'
providesBroadcastService: A BroadcastChannel offers a specific BroadcastService. Also called 'channel offers service', 'service on channel'. Examples: 'Channel 5 provides the 'Evening News BroadcastService'.' 'This broadcast channel provides 'Sports Live'.' 'The channel offers the 'Kids TV Show' broadcast service.'
providesService: A ServiceChannel offers a specific Service. Also called 'channel offers service', 'service via channel'. Examples: 'The online portal provides the 'Customer Support' service.' 'This service channel provides 'Technical Assistance'.' 'The mobile app provides the 'Order Tracking' service.'
publicAccess: A Place is open to public visitors, indicated by a Boolean value. Also called 'open to public', 'publicly accessible'. Examples: 'The park has public access set to true.' 'The private club has public access set to false.' 'The museum indicates public access is true.'
publicTransportClosuresInfo: A SpecialAnnouncement includes URL or WebContent providing information about public transport closures. Also called 'transport closure details', 'public transit alerts'. Examples: 'The announcement includes public transport closures info at 'https://example.com/transport-alerts'.' 'The special announcement provides public transport closures info as a detailed web page.'
publication: A CreativeWork is associated with a PublicationEvent. Also called 'published in', 'event of publication'. Examples: 'The article has a publication event in 'Journal of Science'.' 'The book's publication was a major event.' 'The research paper is linked to a specific publication event.'
publicationType: A MedicalScholarlyArticle is categorized by a Text-based publication type from the US NLM MeSH catalog. Also called 'article type', 'MeSH publication type'. Examples: 'The medical article's publication type is 'Journal Article'.' 'This is a 'Review' publication type.' 'The publication type is 'Clinical Trial'.' 'The publication type is 'Case Report'.'
publishedBy: A PublicationEvent is associated with an Organization or Person responsible for publishing. Also called 'publisher of event', 'issued by'. Examples: 'The publication event was published by 'Springer Nature'.' 'The book launch was published by 'Penguin Random House'.' 'The journal issue was published by 'Dr. Jane Doe'.' 'The event was published by 'Academic Press'.'
publishedOn: A PublicationEvent is associated with a BroadcastService on which it was published. Also called 'broadcast on', 'aired on'. Examples: 'The publication event was published on 'BBC One'.' 'The news segment was published on 'CNN Breaking News'.' 'The special report was published on 'PBS'.'
publisher: A CreativeWork or FinancialIncentive is published by an Organization or Person. Also called 'issued by', 'creator of content'. Examples: 'The book's publisher is 'Penguin Random House'.' 'The article's publisher is 'The New York Times'.' 'The financial incentive is published by 'Bank of America'.' 'The research paper's publisher is 'Elsevier'.' Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a PublicationEvent.
publisherImprint: A CreativeWork (specifically a comic) is published by a specific publishing division or Organization. Also called 'imprint of publisher', 'comic imprint'. Examples: 'The comic was published under the publisher imprint 'Vertigo'.' 'This graphic novel's publisher imprint is 'Image Comics'.' 'The manga series was released under the 'Shonen Jump' imprint.'
publishingPrinciples: A CreativeWork, Organization, or Person adheres to specific publishing principles, described by a CreativeWork or URL. Also called 'editorial guidelines', 'ethics policy', 'content standards'. Examples: 'The organization's publishing principles are outlined at 'https://example.com/ethics'.' 'The news article follows the publishing principles described in their 'Editorial Policy' document.' 'The blog post adheres to the author's publishing principles.'
purchaseDate: A Product or Vehicle was acquired by its current owner on a specific Date. Also called 'date acquired', 'date bought'. Examples: 'The car's purchase date was 2022-07-01.' 'The smartphone's purchase date was 2023-03-10.' 'The antique vase has a purchase date of 1998-11-05.'
purchasePriceLimit: A FinancialIncentive has an optional MonetaryAmount as the maximum price an item can have to qualify. Also called 'maximum price for offer', 'price cap'. Examples: 'The incentive has a purchase price limit of $500.' 'The offer applies to items with a purchase price limit of €100.' 'The discount is valid for products up to a purchase price limit of £75.'
purchaseType: A FinancialIncentive specifies the optional PurchaseTypeEnumeration required for the consumer to qualify. Also called 'type of purchase required'. Examples: 'The incentive requires a purchase type of 'new customer'.' 'This offer has a purchase type of 'online only'.' 'The discount applies to a purchase type of 'in-store'.' 'The incentive is for a purchase type of 'subscription'.' 'The incentive is for a purchase type of 'first-time buyer'.'
qualifications: A JobPosting or Occupation requires specific Credential or Text-based qualifications. Also called 'required skills', 'eligibility criteria', 'credentials needed'. Examples: 'The job posting requires qualifications including a 'Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science'.' 'The occupation demands qualifications such as '5 years of experience in project management'.' 'The role requires 'PMP Certification' as a qualification.' 'The job requires 'excellent communication skills'.' 'The occupation requires 'proficiency in Python'.'
qualifiedExpense: A FinancialIncentive specifies the IncentiveQualifiedExpenseType for expenses covered by the incentive. Also called 'covered expenses', 'eligible costs'. Examples: 'The incentive covers qualified expenses for 'goods'.' 'This offer applies to qualified expenses for 'services'.' 'The incentive is valid for qualified expenses of 'labor'.' 'The incentive covers qualified expenses for 'parts'.'
quarantineGuidelines: A SpecialAnnouncement includes URL or WebContent providing guidelines about quarantine rules. Also called 'quarantine rules', 'isolation guidelines'. Examples: 'The announcement provides quarantine guidelines at 'https://example.com/covid-rules'.' 'The special announcement includes quarantine guidelines as a detailed web page.'
query: A SearchAction uses a Text-based query. Also called 'search term', 'search string'. Examples: 'The search action used the query 'best restaurants near me'.' 'The action's query was 'how to bake bread'.' 'The search action performed the query 'weather forecast'.' 'The search action used the query 'latest news'.'
quest: A Game or VideoGameSeries features a Thing representing a task for players to complete for a reward. Also called 'player mission', 'game objective', 'task'. Examples: 'The video game features a quest to 'defeat the dragon'.' 'The game includes a quest called 'The Lost Artifact'.' 'The series has a quest to 'rescue the princess'.' 'The game has a quest to 'collect 10 coins'.'
question: An AskAction involves a Question. Also called 'inquiry', 'asked question'. Examples: 'The ask action posed the question 'What is the capital of France?'.' 'The action involved the question 'How does this work?'.' 'The ask action presented the question 'Are you available tomorrow?'.'
rangeIncludes: A Property relates to a Class that defines the expected type(s) for its values. Also called 'value type', 'expected type', 'object type'. Examples: 'The 'name' property's range includes 'Text'.' 'The 'author' property's range includes 'Person' or 'Organization'.' 'The 'dateCreated' property's range includes 'Date' or 'DateTime'.'
ratingCount: An AggregateRating indicates the Integer total number of ratings received. Also called 'number of ratings', 'total ratings'. Examples: 'The aggregate rating has a rating count of 150.' 'The product received a rating count of 500.' 'The movie has a rating count of 10,000.'
ratingExplanation: A Rating provides a Text-based short explanation for the conclusion expressed in the rating. Also called 'reason for rating', 'rating context'. Examples: 'The rating explanation states 'The service was prompt and efficient'.' 'The rating includes an explanation: 'The product exceeded expectations'.' 'The rating explanation clarifies 'The delivery was late, but the item was perfect'.'
ratingValue: A Rating expresses its value as a Number or Text. Also called 'score', 'rating score'. Examples: 'The rating value is 4.5.' 'The rating value is 'Excellent'.' 'The rating value is 5 out of 5.' 'The rating value is 8.5.'
readBy: An Audiobook is performed or read by a Person. Also called 'narrated by', 'performed by'. Examples: 'The audiobook is read by 'Morgan Freeman'.' 'This audiobook is read by 'the author'.' 'The story is read by 'a professional voice actor'.'
readonlyValue: A PropertyValueSpecification indicates by a Boolean whether a property's value is mutable. Also called 'immutable property', 'fixed value'. Examples: 'The property has a readonly value of true.' 'The readonly value for this field is false.' 'The property specification indicates readonly value is true.'
realEstateAgent: A RentAction involves a RealEstateAgent as a participant. Also called 'agent involved', 'rental agent'. Examples: 'The rent action involved the real estate agent 'John Smith'.' 'The apartment rental was facilitated by 'Acme Realty'.' 'The real estate agent 'Jane Doe' participated in the rent action.'
recipe: A CookAction uses a Recipe as its instrument. Also called 'cooking instructions', 'recipe used'. Examples: 'The cook action followed the recipe for 'chocolate chip cookies'.' 'The action used the recipe 'Spaghetti Carbonara'.' 'The cook action was guided by the recipe 'Grandma's Apple Pie'.'
recipeCategory: A Recipe belongs to a Text-based category. Also called 'dish category', 'type of recipe'. Examples: 'The recipe category is 'appetizer'.' 'This recipe falls under the 'dessert' category.' 'The recipe category is 'entree'.' 'The recipe category is 'breakfast'.'
recipeCuisine: A Recipe is associated with a Text-based cuisine type. Also called 'cuisine type', 'ethnic cuisine'. Examples: 'The recipe cuisine is 'Italian'.' 'This recipe is of 'Mexican' cuisine.' 'The recipe cuisine is 'French'.' 'The recipe cuisine is 'Ethiopian'.'
recipeIngredient: A Recipe includes an ItemList, PropertyValue, or Text describing its ingredients and quantities. Also called 'ingredients list', 'components'. Examples: 'The recipe ingredient is '1 cup of flour'.' 'The recipe ingredients include '2 large eggs'.' 'The recipe ingredient is 'salt to taste'.' 'The recipe ingredient is 'a pinch of sugar'.'
recipeInstructions: A Recipe provides CreativeWork, ItemList, or Text as steps for making the dish. Also called 'cooking steps', 'preparation guide'. Examples: 'The recipe instructions are a list of steps to follow.' 'The recipe instructions include a video tutorial.' 'The recipe instructions are provided as a detailed text description.'
recipeYield: A Recipe produces a QuantitativeValue or Text indicating the quantity it yields. Also called 'servings', 'output quantity'. Examples: 'The recipe yield is '4 servings'.' 'The recipe yields '12 cookies'.' 'The recipe yield is '2 loaves of bread'.' 'The recipe yield is 'enough for 6 people'.'
recipient: An AuthorizeAction, CommunicateAction, DonateAction, GiveAction, Message, PayAction, ReturnAction, SendAction, or TipAction has an Audience, ContactPoint, Organization, or Person as the receiving end. Also called 'receiver', 'addressee', 'beneficiary'. Examples: 'The message was sent to the recipient 'John Doe'.' 'The payment action's recipient is 'Acme Corp'.' 'The donation was given to the recipient 'Charity Foundation'.' 'The communication action was directed at the recipient 'Customer Support'.'
recognizedBy: A Credential is acknowledged by an Organization. Also called 'accredited by', 'validated by'. Examples: 'The certification is recognized by 'ISO'.' 'The degree is recognized by 'the Department of Education'.' 'The credential is recognized by 'Professional Association X'.'
recognizingAuthority: A MedicalEntity is officially recognized by an Organization as part of its endorsed system of medicine. Also called 'official authority', 'endorsing body'. Examples: 'The medical entity is recognized by the 'World Health Organization'.' 'The treatment is recognized by the 'American Medical Association'.' 'The recognizing authority for this therapy is 'National Health Service'.'
recommendationStrength: A MedicalGuidelineRecommendation indicates its strength as Text. Also called 'strength of recommendation', 'guideline strength'. Examples: 'The recommendation strength is 'class I'.' 'The guideline has a recommendation strength of 'strong'.' 'The recommendation strength is 'moderate'.' 'The recommendation strength is 'weak'.'
recommendedIntake: A DietarySupplement has a RecommendedDoseSchedule for its intake for a given population. Also called 'suggested dosage', 'dosage instructions'. Examples: 'The dietary supplement has a recommended intake of '2 capsules daily'.' 'The recommended intake is 'one tablet with food'.' 'The supplement's recommended intake is 'as directed by a physician'.'
recordLabel: A MusicRelease was issued by an Organization acting as its record label. Also called 'label', 'issued by label'. Examples: 'The music release was issued by the record label 'Universal Music Group'.' 'The album's record label is 'Sony Music'.' 'The single was released by the record label 'Atlantic Records'.'
recordedAs: A MusicComposition has an audio recording represented by a MusicRecording. Also called 'audio version', 'recorded performance'. Examples: 'The music composition is recorded as 'Symphony No. 5 by Beethoven'.' 'This composition has a recorded as 'Live at Carnegie Hall'.' 'The song is recorded as 'Studio Version 2023'.'
recordedAt: A CreativeWork was recorded at an Event. Also called 'recorded during', 'captured at event'. Examples: 'The concert film was recorded at the 'Live Aid' event.' 'The documentary was recorded at the 'Science Fair'.' 'The interview was recorded at the 'Tech Conference'.' 'The performance was recorded at the 'Music Festival'.'
recordedIn: An Event was captured, in whole or in part, by a CreativeWork. Also called 'captured by', 'documented in'. Examples: 'The concert event was recorded in the 'Live Album'.' 'The historical event was recorded in the 'Documentary Film'.' 'The conference was recorded in the 'Event Proceedings'.' 'The speech was recorded in the 'Audio Recording'.'
recordingOf: A MusicRecording is a recording of a specific MusicComposition. Also called 'version of composition', 'performance of'. Examples: 'The music recording is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.' 'This track is a recording of 'Bohemian Rhapsody'.' 'The recording is of 'Moonlight Sonata'.' Distinct from recordedAs, which links a composition to its recording.
recourseLoan: A LoanOrCredit is a recourse loan, indicated by a Boolean, meaning the lender can pursue the borrower for remaining debt after collateral is seized. Also called 'full recourse loan', 'borrower liable'. Examples: 'The loan is a recourse loan, set to true.' 'The mortgage is a recourse loan, meaning the borrower is still liable.' 'The loan has recourse loan set to false, indicating non-recourse.'
referee: A SportsEvent involves a Person acting as an official to enforce rules. Also called 'umpire', 'judge', 'official'. Examples: 'The football match had 'Pierluigi Collina' as the referee.' 'The tennis game's referee was 'Eva Asderaki-Moore'.' 'The boxing match had 'Joe Cortez' as the referee.'
referenceQuantity: A UnitPriceSpecification uses a QuantitativeValue as the quantity for which a certain price applies. Also called 'base quantity for price', 'price per quantity'. Examples: 'The price applies to a reference quantity of '4 kWh'.' 'The unit price is for a reference quantity of '1 liter'.' 'The price is based on a reference quantity of '100 grams'.'
referencesOrder: An Invoice is related to one or more Order(s). Also called 'invoice for order', 'order linked to invoice'. Examples: 'The invoice references order 'ORD-2023-001'.' 'The invoice references orders 'ORD-2023-002' and 'ORD-2023-003'.' 'The invoice is for the order 'Customer Order 123'.'
refundType: A MerchantReturnPolicy or MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride specifies a RefundTypeEnumeration. Also called 'type of refund', 'refund method'. Examples: 'The return policy specifies a refund type of 'full refund'.' 'The policy allows a refund type of 'store credit'.' 'The refund type is 'exchange only'.' 'The refund type is 'partial refund'.'
regionDrained: A LymphaticVessel or Vein drains an AnatomicalStructure or AnatomicalSystem. Also called 'drains area', 'supplies drainage to'. Examples: 'The lymphatic vessel drains the 'upper limb region'.' 'The vein drains the 'digestive system'.' 'The vessel drains the 'thoracic cavity'.' 'The vein drains the 'brain'.'
regionsAllowed: A MediaObject is permitted in specific Place regions. Also called 'allowed in regions', 'geographical availability'. Examples: 'The media object is allowed in regions 'US, CA'.' 'The video is allowed in regions 'Europe'.' 'The content is allowed in regions 'Japan'.' 'The media is allowed in regions 'Worldwide'.'
relatedAnatomy: SuperficialAnatomy relates to specific AnatomicalStructure or AnatomicalSystem. Also called 'associated anatomy', 'connected to anatomy'. Examples: 'The superficial anatomy relates to the 'musculoskeletal system'.' 'The skin condition relates to the 'epidermis'.' 'The superficial anatomy is related to the 'nervous system'.' 'The superficial anatomy is related to the 'lymphatic system'.'
relatedCondition: An AnatomicalStructure, AnatomicalSystem, or SuperficialAnatomy is associated with a MedicalCondition. Also called 'associated condition', 'condition linked to'. Examples: 'The anatomical structure is associated with the related condition 'arthritis'.' 'The digestive system has a related condition of 'Crohn's disease'.' 'The superficial anatomy is linked to the related condition 'eczema'.' 'The anatomical system has a related condition of 'diabetes'.'
relatedDrug: A Drug has other Drug(s) related to it, such as alternatives. Also called 'alternative drug', 'similar medication'. Examples: 'The drug has a related drug 'ibuprofen'.' 'This medication has related drugs like 'acetaminophen'.' 'The related drug is 'generic version X'.' 'The related drug is 'Drug B'.'
relatedLink: A WebPage has a URL that is a related link. Also called 'associated link', 'external link'. Examples: 'The web page includes a related link to 'https://example.com/more-info'.' 'The article has a related link to 'another relevant page'.' 'The web page provides a related link to 'a partner website'.'
relatedStructure: An AnatomicalSystem has AnatomicalStructure(s) that are not part of the system but connect to it. Also called 'connected structures', 'associated structures'. Examples: 'The circulatory system has related structures like 'capillaries'.' 'The nervous system has related structures such as 'sensory receptors'.'
